title: Ripple Targets High-Value Real Estate Deals With New Crypto Partnership
summary: Cryptocurrency holders could gain a smoother route to property purchases through a new partnership between Ripple and Cryptescrow. The collaboration aims to support high-value closings while preserving the procedures used by sellers, developers, and title companies. Ripple Partnership Targets High-V...
content:
Cryptocurrency holders could gain a smoother route to property purchases through a new partnership between Ripple and Cryptescrow. The collaboration aims to support high-value closings while preserving the procedures used by sellers, developers, and title companies.

Key Takeaways

  • The partnership targets high-value purchases funded with cryptocurrency.
  • Cryptescrow converts buyers’ digital holdings into U.S. dollars.
  • Ripple previously supported tokenized property deeds and trading in Dubai.

Ripple Partnership Targets High-Value Home Purchases

Homebuyers holding cryptocurrency could find it easier to fund property purchases through a partnership designed to connect digital assets with conventional real estate closings. Real estate settlement provider Cryptescrow announced its strategic partnership with Ripple on Oct. 22, drawing on the blockchain financial technology company’s experience serving businesses and institutions.

Under the model described in the announcement, Cryptescrow converts cryptocurrency into U.S. dollars for property purchases. Sellers, developers, title companies, and other closing participants would continue handling conventional funds. The collaboration will support efforts to handle large transactions while maintaining compliance, transparency, and security throughout the closing process.

The arrangement focuses on buyers with substantial holdings of cryptocurrency that can be exchanged or used for payments. Cryptescrow founder and CEO John Ioannou Jr., a real estate attorney, said:

“Ripple has spent years working on the connection between blockchain technology and traditional financial systems. Real estate is a natural next step for that infrastructure, particularly as more buyers want to use digital assets without forcing everyone else involved in the closing to change how they operate.”

An earlier transaction illustrates the conversion model in practice: a First American Title policy-issuing agent closed a $4.2 million residential purchase in which the buyer used Cryptescrow’s conversion process, the company reported Aug. 10. Its service is available as an optional offering to those agents, who independently evaluate its suitability for eligible transactions.

In September, Cryptescrow also announced a partnership with crypto exchange Kraken to access trading infrastructure for luxury and commercial property purchases. The arrangement uses Kraken’s professional trading desk to support large conversions.

Earlier Ripple Deals Span Dubai Property Tokens and Stablecoins

Ripple’s involvement in real estate predates the Cryptescrow partnership through its work with tokenization infrastructure provider Ctrl Alt in Dubai. In July 2025, the companies partnered to support custody of tokenized property title deeds issued on the XRP Ledger for the Dubai Land Department’s project.

By February, the Dubai initiative had progressed to controlled secondary trading of tokenized properties, allowing eligible interests to be resold. That project concerns digital property ownership records and trading, while the Cryptescrow collaboration addresses funding conventional purchases with cryptocurrency.

Beyond real estate, Ripple’s settlement work with Bitso targets dollar-peso liquidity using stablecoins. The initiative focuses on institutional payments across the U.S.-Mexico corridor, extending the company’s efforts to connect digital assets with conventional currencies.

Standard Chartered separately opened custody for Ripple USD (RLUSD) on the XRP Ledger on Oct. 12. Eligible institutions can safeguard the dollar-backed token through the bank’s digital asset custody service.

title: Aave Opens Its First Externally Curated V4 Markets With Sentora
summary: Sentora is managing Aave V4’s first externally curated markets, bringing a new division of lending strategy, liquidity and governance controls to Ethereum.
content:
Aave’s first externally curated V4 markets are live on Ethereum, according to Sentora’s October 22 launch explanation. The curator says it is managing active borrowing markets for RLUSD, PYUSD and OUSD within a governance-approved deployment.

TL;DR: Aave’s first externally curated V4 markets are live on Ethereum with Sentora managing strategy and risk settings. Borrowing options include RLUSD, PYUSD and OUSD.

Sentora manages collateral rules, risk parameters, interest-rate curves and oracle configurations. Those responsibilities put practical decisions about lending conditions with an outside specialist while retaining the framework of Aave governance.

Shared Liquidity, Different Lending Rules

Aave V4 divides the system between hubs and spokes. The protocol’s liquidity documentation describes a hub as the central settlement and accounting layer holding assets. Spokes are specialized smart contracts through which users interact with a market’s collateral, borrowing and liquidation logic.

This arrangement lets different markets draw on an underlying liquidity pool while applying different conditions. Governance controls how much capacity a spoke receives. Credit limits constrain borrowing, and supply limits constrain additions, giving the system ways to limit activity without requiring every market to use the same collateral policy.

For a borrower, that makes the identity of the market relevant. Two markets built on the same protocol can offer different assets, borrowing capacity and liquidation conditions. A shared brand or common liquidity source alone does not establish that their positions will behave alike during a sharp market move.

For suppliers, the practical comparison is between the income offered and the market rules that produce it. A higher rate can be attractive, but it also makes it important to inspect which borrowers can access the liquidity and what happens if collateral values deteriorate.

A New Layer To Monitor

Sentora has also extended its Risk Radar to cover the V4 structure. The monitoring system separates hub, spoke and asset views, with tools for comparing caps against usage and showing where borrowing is concentrated. A governance tracker records changes to assets and parameters.

The company gives a practical example of how a limit works: a spoke that reaches its borrowing cap cannot draw additional funds until capacity becomes available through repayment or an approved increase. That restriction is relevant even when users can see liquidity elsewhere in the wider system.

For DeFi users assessing the new markets, the launch creates another set of decisions to examine. The curator’s collateral choices matter alongside the protocol’s contract design; the market’s allocated capacity matters alongside the total liquidity headline. Monitoring can make those differences visible, although a dashboard cannot remove losses from an unsuitable collateral policy.

The first rollout provides a live test of that division of responsibility: Sentora sets market strategy, Aave supplies the lending framework, and governance determines the boundaries within which the markets operate.

Written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

title: Tell Me Lies: Grok, GPT and Claude Voice Modes Guess Bitcoin’s Price
summary: Can artificial intelligence (AI) think as well out loud as it does in writing? A bitcoin forecasting experiment conducted by Bitcoin.com News put ChatGPT, Grok, and Claude Opus 5.5 to the test, exposing shaky predictions, questionable reasoning, and a surprising twist: Claude’s voice model proved mo...
content:
Can artificial intelligence (AI) think as well out loud as it does in writing? A bitcoin forecasting experiment conducted by Bitcoin.com News put ChatGPT, Grok, and Claude Opus 5.5 to the test, exposing shaky predictions, questionable reasoning, and a surprising twist: Claude’s voice model proved more transparent about its limitations than its text-based counterpart.

Key Takeaways

  • ChatGPT and Grok voice both finished at $82,000, but their explanations contained important weaknesses.
  • Claude Opus 5.5 voice disclosed limitations sooner than its text session, which predicted $78,000.
  • All 4 AI sessions lacked reproducible price calculations, leaving voice-versus-text accuracy unresolved.

The Experiment That Put AI’s Talking and Typing Skills to the Test

Artificial intelligence (AI) can carry on a conversation, sound like a financial analyst, and deliver a bitcoin price prediction without missing a beat. But does speaking to an AI produce the same quality of reasoning as typing a question into one? An Oct. 23, 2026, experiment put that question to the test, and the answers were anything but straightforward.

ChatGPT and Grok were questioned through voice interfaces, while Claude Opus 5.5 initially worked through text. A subsequent Claude Opus 5.5 voice session added a revealing comparison. All four delivered specific year-end bitcoin prices. None demonstrated a reproducible calculation behind its final number, but the differences in factual accuracy, consistency, and willingness to admit uncertainty were striking.

Four Sessions, Three AI Companies and One Bitcoin Question

The exercise involved OpenAI’s ChatGPT, xAI’s Grok, and Anthropic’s Claude Opus 5.5. Each was asked to predict bitcoin’s closing price on Dec. 31, 2026, using five prompts that emphasized historical cycles, onchain activity, institutional adoption, and economic conditions.

Bitcoin was trading near $81,200 on Oct. 23, giving the experiment a common market reference. ChatGPT’s voice session started at $89,500 and eventually settled on $82,000. Grok’s spoken estimate moved from $88,000 to $82,000. Claude’s text model maintained $78,000 across its prompts, while its later voice session began at $88,000 before holding at $85,000.

The exercise wasn’t a controlled scientific benchmark. Different companies use different architectures, and the sessions did not have identical verified access to live information. Nevertheless, the conversations offered a revealing look at how convincingly these systems can present financial reasoning and how well that reasoning survives scrutiny.

ChatGPT’s Voice Sounded Busy, but the Numbers Kept Moving

ChatGPT’s voice session produced one of the experiment’s clearest examples of conversational fluency, getting well ahead of demonstrated analysis. Its forecast changed from $89,500 to $86,500 after Bitcoin.com News introduced additional analytical factors. Another spoken prompt left the number unchanged, but a later question concerning an 18- to 24-month outlook brought the prediction down to $82,000.

The review found no evidence of fresh market retrieval between those revisions. Instead, the changes followed shifts in how the questions were framed. The spoken language made the process sound more substantial than it actually was. ChatGPT’s model in voice mode used expressions including “let me pull those pieces together” and “Checking that now.” Those phrases ordinarily suggest that someone is consulting information. The experiment did not establish that any such research occurred. It seemed to be lying.

A subsequent text-based ChatGPT conversation offered a more skeptical assessment of the earlier voice exchange, including the admission, “I treated plausibility as evidence.” That distinction matters because ChatGPT’s voice and text experiences can use different underlying models. The text assistant’s later explanation cannot, by itself, establish precisely what the voice system did internally.

The episode showed how easily a natural-sounding conversation can create an impression of investigative work, even when the resulting answer provides little evidence of it.

Grok’s Voice Delivered Details but Got a Crucial Number Backward

Grok’s spoken responses sounded more thoroughly researched, supplying figures about bitcoin’s historical declines, inflation, institutional activity, and the recent Mt Gox repayment delay. Much of that information matched the facts and sources. Then came a doozy. Grok reportedly assigned roughly 90% probability to a Federal Reserve rate hike at the Oct. 27-28 meeting. The review’s market references instead placed those odds around 6% to 18%, depending on the source and observation date.

The difference was substantial. It essentially grabbed from an older reference point. A low-probability interest rate increase had been presented as something close to a certainty. Other problems included a stale $150,000 Bernstein bitcoin target and an incorrect description of where Fidelity’s projected price range stood relative to the market. Grok eventually corrected its rate probabilities, but only after being challenged.

Its later claim that it hadn’t retrieved live data was also difficult to reconcile with its references to recent inflation and Mt Gox developments. The subsequent questioning could not establish whether that information came from retrieval, prior context, or another source. For the voice comparison, the important finding wasn’t simply that Grok made an error. It was that correct and incorrect financial claims arrived with essentially the same conversational confidence.

Claude’s Text Model Searched for Evidence but Still Invented a Method

Claude Opus 5.5’s original text session had a documented advantage: It performed four web searches before answering. Its $78,000 prediction drew partly on bitcoin’s True Market Mean, estimated near $77,600. That gave the response a concrete market reference, something the ChatGPT voice session largely lacked. Yet the written answer had problems of its own.

Claude misstated historical halving-cycle timing, understated bitcoin’s roughly 54% peak-to-trough decline, and omitted the Iran war’s oil shock from its economic discussion. It also favored an exchange-traded fund outflow narrative despite retrieving information indicating a different picture for October. More revealing was how the system described its work.

Claude referred to “Data points I weighted most heavily” and claimed to have priced a December rate increase into its forecast. Under further questioning, however, it acknowledged that it hadn’t computed numerical weights or probabilities. The $78,000 estimate was a judgment anchored to a market measure, not the output of a demonstrated quantitative model.

It took three rounds of questioning before Claude’s text session adequately separated sourced information from unsupported assumptions. Web retrieval had provided more material to discuss, but it hadn’t guaranteed sound analysis.

Claude’s Voice Model Delivered the Experiment’s Biggest Surprise

The latter Claude Opus 5.5 voice session changed the comparison. Its initial prediction was $88,000, subsequently revised to $85,000. Unlike ChatGPT’s voice session, which changed its answer multiple times, Claude held that revised figure through the remaining prompts and resisted adjusting it merely to produce a more attention-grabbing forecast.

More importantly, Claude’s voice response volunteered limitations earlier than the other sessions. During its second answer, it acknowledged that it couldn’t pull live onchain metrics and described its prediction as an estimate rather than a calculated model output. When asked to identify unsupported information, it separated retrieved figures, general knowledge, calculations and opinions on the first request.

That was a better disclosure performance than Claude’s own text session, which required three rounds of questioning to reach a comparable level of candor. The spoken model also correctly described historical Bitcoin cycle peaks as generally occurring 12 to 18 months after halvings, avoiding a timing error made by both Grok’s voice session and Claude’s original text response.

Still, Claude’s voice performance was hardly flawless. It cited oil above $110 using a figure the review considered outdated, overstated continuing institutional bitcoin purchases and omitted the deeper June 2026 market decline when discussing the current drawdown. It also never showed a calculation producing its $85,000 target.

The surprise, then, wasn’t that Claude’s voice model became a better financial forecaster. It was that, in this particular session, the spoken assistant was more forthcoming about its limitations than its text counterpart.

Why Voice and Text AI Aren’t Necessarily the Same System

The comparison raises a technical issue that casual users may never consider: Speaking to an AI isn’t always equivalent to typing into it. OpenAI’s ChatGPT voice experience uses a separate model family from its primary text experience. Anthropic, meanwhile, describes Claude voice as operating through the fastest version of the selected model, including supported Sonnet and Opus options.

That difference complicates straightforward comparisons. Even when the interface displays the same model name, the voice experience may involve different execution settings, latency constraints and speech-processing components. The experiment did not independently establish how those factors affected the answers.

Grok’s voice architecture was not verified in the report, leaving another important piece of the technical comparison unresolved. The sessions, therefore, cannot establish that voice AI is inherently less accurate, more prone to fabrication, or more transparent than generative text AI. What they show is that the interface and underlying configuration matter, and that a familiar brand name alone does not guarantee equivalent behavior.

Claude provided the most useful within-company comparison, but even there, the text and voice sessions occurred separately and did not constitute repeated, controlled trials.

The Real Test Comes After the AI Stops Talking

Across the four sessions, the final forecasts ranged from $78,000 to $85,000, all relatively close to bitcoin’s prevailing market price. None demonstrated how its assumptions translated into the exact figure it selected. The review also identified limitations in its own methodology. Claude authored the assessment of its performance, and several market claims were checked through search excerpts rather than complete primary sources.

No independent tool logs established precisely what each voice assistant retrieved. Those qualifications are essential, but only open to xAI, OpenAI, and Anthropic. This was an exploratory experiment, not proof that one company or interaction mode consistently outperforms another. But it did expose an important difference between sounding analytical and showing actual analysis.

Voice assistants can deliver financial commentary with the rhythm and assurance of a professional broadcaster. Text models can assemble detailed explanations supported by retrieved sources. Either can still produce an unsupported conclusion, hallucinations or downright lies, and either can improve when pressed to distinguish evidence from inference.

Claude’s later voice session showed that speaking to an AI doesn’t automatically mean sacrificing transparency. At the same time, ChatGPT and Grok showed why polished spoken answers deserve the same scrutiny as written ones. For anyone using AI to evaluate investments, the next test should require identical prompts, documented retrieval activity, repeated sessions, and independently checked figures.

Only then can researchers begin separating the effects of voice interaction from the underlying model’s reasoning capabilities. The experiment’s most revealing result wasn’t whether bitcoin would finish 2026 at $78,000, $82,000 or $85,000. It was that four convincing performances in voice mode produced four sets of financial reasoning, and not one could show the math behind its final answer.

title: Circle Gateway Adds Bitcoin And Euro Balances With cirBTC And EURC
summary: Circle has expanded Gateway to cirBTC and EURC, bringing bitcoin and euro assets into its unified-balance system with different network and payment limits.
content:
Circle is taking its cross-chain balance service beyond USDC. The company announced on October 23 that Gateway now supports its wrapped Bitcoin token, cirBTC, and euro stablecoin EURC, giving developers a common interface for moving three different assets.

TL;DR: Gateway now supports cirBTC and EURC alongside USDC, with separate balances and different network routes. Its advertised speed applies after deposits have finalized.

The Euro And Bitcoin Routes Differ

The expansion has a narrower footprint for bitcoin than for euros. Circle’s asset-support documentation lists cirBTC on Arc and Ethereum. EURC is supported on Arc, Avalanche, Base, Ethereum, Solana and World Chain. Availability of a token elsewhere does not automatically make that network a Gateway route.

Each asset retains its own balance. Depositing EURC creates access to EURC across its supported networks; it does not fund a cirBTC withdrawal or convert euros into dollars. Applications still need a separate exchange operation when the underlying asset changes.

That distinction matters for the kinds of businesses the service could help. A payments firm serving euro customers on several networks could, in principle, reduce the amount of EURC it parks in separate places. The design simplifies where a balance can be used while leaving currency exposure and conversion decisions with the business.

The Speed Claim Starts After Finality

Circle advertises cross-chain access in less than 500 milliseconds once a balance has been established. That condition excludes the time needed for a fresh deposit to reach finality on its source network. A customer moving funds into Gateway for the first time therefore faces a different timing calculation from an application spending an existing balance.

The Gateway documentation describes deposits held in noncustodial GatewayWallet escrow contracts. An authorized request then allows the same asset to be minted on a supported destination chain. Circle also provides a withdrawal path that does not depend on its API, although that route carries a seven-day delay. Control of funds and immediate access to funds are separate considerations.

The new assets also work with Circle’s Nanopayments system, which groups off-chain payments for settlement in batches. Support has an additional boundary here: nanopayments involving assets other than USDC are limited to Ethereum Virtual Machine networks. EURC’s Gateway availability on Solana should not be read as EURC Nanopayments support there.

Circle says it is waiving Gateway fees for cirBTC and EURC on Arc at launch. Developers still need to assess the full transaction path, including deposits, withdrawals and settlement. Eliminating a gas charge for each individual payment does not eliminate the cost of every batch or every interaction with a smart contract.

For prospective users, the useful test is concrete: whether the required asset, destination network and payment method all appear in the supported combination. A unified interface makes those decisions easier to implement, but the route matrix still determines what an application can deliver.

Written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

title: Nasdaq-Listed XRP Firm Evernorth Puts 13-Year-Old Wallet in Spotlight
summary: Evernorth is drawing on Fuzzybear’s early XRP history for a limited merchandise collaboration. The initiative connects a publicly traded treasury company with supporters who built a community around the wallet and its symbolic trading order. Fuzzybear’s 2014 Offer Becomes Part of XRP History A walle...
content:
Evernorth is drawing on Fuzzybear’s early XRP history for a limited merchandise collaboration. The initiative connects a publicly traded treasury company with supporters who built a community around the wallet and its symbolic trading order.

Key Takeaways

  • Evernorth and the Fuzzies plan co-branded merchandise for Fuzzycon.
  • The company puts Fuzzy community participation above 20,000.
  • The collaboration does not constitute an endorsement of $FUZZY.

Fuzzybear’s 2014 Offer Becomes Part of XRP History

A wallet activated in 2013 inspired a limited merchandise release that Evernorth Holdings Inc. (Nasdaq: XRPN) announced Oct. 22. Sagar Shah, chief business officer, outlined the Evernorth x Fuzzy collaboration as recognition for longtime supporters. Fuzzybear is the historical wallet’s name; the Fuzzies are the community formed around its story.

Fuzzybear was activated on Feb. 21, 2013, approximately eight months after the XRP Ledger launched in June 2012.

On Jan. 1, 2014, Fuzzybear placed its historical XRP trading order, offering 1 XRP for 1 Bitstamp-issued BTC through the ledger’s built-in decentralized exchange. The company interprets the offer as confidence in XRP’s faster settlement, lower fees, and native trading capabilities compared with earlier blockchains. Its chief business officer wrote:

“The Fuzzies are a reminder of the types of community members who helped us get to where we are now.”

Community Builds Around Art, Cards, and Meetups

Longtime ecosystem participants established the Fuzzies in January 2025, adopting a scruffy bear mascot and developing tokens, artwork, trading cards, and gatherings. Evernorth puts participation at more than 20,000 across X, Telegram, and the ledger. The group combines shared interests in cryptocurrency and blockchain with physical collectibles and social events.

Earlier recognition efforts included Evernorth’s XRP community campaign, featuring Bearchamp, a boxing bear character created by Chicago artist JC Rivera. The latest release coincides with Swell 2026 week, Ripple’s annual finance and blockchain conference in New York. The limited merchandise will carry both Evernorth and Fuzzy branding.

Fuzzybear ($FUZZY) is a community token issued on the XRP Ledger to commemorate the historical wallet. It is distinct from XRP, the network’s native cryptocurrency. Evernorth states that it does not endorse, sponsor, or promote $FUZZY, other digital assets, or non-fungible tokens (NFTs), unique blockchain tokens that can represent collectibles or other items.

The company also discloses that XRP is its primary treasury asset and that increases in its value may benefit the business.

Fuzzycon Brings the Collaboration to New York

Public-market trading in Evernorth shares began Oct. 12, giving stock investors exposure to its actively managed XRP treasury. The Nasdaq trading debut followed a merger with Armada Acquisition Corp. II, a special purpose acquisition company formed to take another business public. Evernorth reported approximately 473 million XRP at the transaction’s closing.

Company leadership subsequently marked the listing with a ceremony at Nasdaq Marketsite in New York’s Times Square on Oct. 14. Alongside the Nasdaq closing-bell celebration, Evernorth outlined an objective of increasing XRP held per share through investment strategies, ecosystem participation, and capital markets activities.

Scheduled for Oct. 26, the first Fuzzycon gathering will bring Fuzzy and wider XRP community participants to Creature’s Rooftop in New York City from 5 to 11 p.m. Organizers list free admission, card games, merchandise, and giveaways. Guests must be at least 21 and present valid photo identification. Capacity is limited to 150 people at a time.

title: Stellar Updates Bell Upgrade Guide Ahead Of November Votes
summary: Stellar’s October 23 Bell guide update sets out software preparation for November votes, with new address handling and ledger decoding requirements.
content:
Stellar has updated its Bell upgrade guide with the software versions that wallets, exchanges and infrastructure operators need before November’s network votes. The October 23 update adds concrete release references as teams prepare for changes to addresses and ledger data under Protocol 30.

TL;DR: Stellar’s updated Bell guide identifies software needed before November’s upgrade votes. Applications must handle new addresses and ledger formats; network activation remains conditional.

The Stellar Development Foundation’s revised guide lists infrastructure releases and software development kits, along with tracking links for community-maintained tools. That gives operators a version checklist for work that must happen before the network adopts the changes.

New Addresses Need Application Support

The JavaScript SDK v17.3.0 release, published October 21, supplies support for contract addresses beginning with W and updated ledger definitions. Its release notes include tools to encode, decode and validate those addresses, plus transfer handling. That version was already available when the readiness guide was updated two days later.

Under Bell, a contract address can carry an additional customer identifier. The foundation’s technical announcement explains that this lets one smart contract receive funds for multiple customers while recording which customer a payment belongs to. It extends an arrangement already available for classic Stellar accounts.

For a custody service, that could simplify a shared account structure. The application still has to recognize the new address and associate the identifier with the right customer. Installing a library capable of reading the address does not, by itself, change every validation or bookkeeping rule built around it.

There is a second preparation task for indexers, explorers and other services that read raw ledger data. Protocol 30 changes the ledger header format. The guide warns that decoders using older definitions will fail on the new values, making compatibility work relevant beyond businesses adopting the new address feature.

Quantum Verification Has A Limited Scope

Bell also adds support for ML-DSA signature verification inside smart contracts. That can support custom accounts using post-quantum authorization, but ordinary network transaction signatures remain Ed25519. The change supplies a building block for developers rather than completing a network-wide cryptographic migration.

A separate change introduces millisecond ledger timestamps. The foundation says this removes a technical barrier to faster ledger closing in future steps. Bell alone does not reduce the current interval. Applications should also avoid assuming that consecutive ledgers must have different whole-second timestamps.

Some tooling is still being finalized: the guide lists the Protocol 30 command-line release as pending and the Soroban Rust SDK as a release candidate. Testnet validators are scheduled to vote November 3, followed by a mainnet vote November 23, both at 17:00 UTC. The upgrade takes effect if validators approve, and the foundation says dates can change.

Written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

title: Gold Bugs Meet Their Worst Nightmare: A Machine That Prints Gold
summary: A San Francisco startup claims it has turned mercury into real gold, beating CERN’s production rate by ten times. The nuclear feat comes as gold trades just under $4,000 an ounce, roughly 26% below its January peak, raising questions about future scarcity. Marathon Fusion Claims a Breakthrough in Go...
content:
A San Francisco startup claims it has turned mercury into real gold, beating CERN’s production rate by ten times. The nuclear feat comes as gold trades just under $4,000 an ounce, roughly 26% below its January peak, raising questions about future scarcity.

Key Takeaways

  • Marathon Fusion claims it converted mercury into stable gold, beating CERN’s production rate by ten times.
  • Gold closed near $3,996 on Oct. 23, approximately 26% below its January peak amid broader market weakness.
  • World Gold Council estimates put above-ground gold stocks at 222,600 tonnes, dwarfing laboratory production.

Marathon Fusion Claims a Breakthrough in Gold Production

Marathon Fusion announced this week that it had demonstrated a process for converting mercury into stable gold, using nuclear reactions rather than the mythical chemistry pursued by medieval alchemists.

The company, founded in 2023, shared gamma-ray measurements it said supported the experiment. However, according to several reports, including from the Financial Times (FT), Marathon Fusion hasn’t disclosed how much gold it produced, what it cost, or whether anyone independently verified the results.

The physics isn’t science fiction. Marathon’s July 2025 research proposed bombarding mercury-198 with high-energy neutrons inside a fusion reactor, creating mercury-197, which subsequently decays into gold-197, the stable isotope found in jewelry, coins, and central-bank vaults. Its simulations projected approximately two tonnes of gold annually per gigawatt of thermal fusion power. That’s theoretical industrial output, not demonstrated production.

CERN’s Gold Experiment Sets a Microscopic Benchmark

Marathon’s claim of beating CERN by 10 times sounds extraordinary until the original benchmark enters the picture. In 2025, CERN researchers reported that lead collisions at the Large Hadron Collider generated approximately 86 billion gold nuclei between 2015 and 2018. Their combined mass amounted to just 29 picograms, or 29 trillionths of a gram.

Even multiplying that quantity by 10 yields only 290 picograms, although Marathon’s production-rate comparison doesn’t establish its actual output. Neither experiment demonstrated commercially viable gold production. Radioactive byproducts, costly equipment, and complex isotope separation present additional obstacles.

Gold Trades Below $4,000 as Supply Questions Emerge

The scientific claim arrives during a difficult stretch for gold investors. The precious metal finished Friday, Oct. 23, near $3,995 per troy ounce, down approximately 0.7% on the day and 4% over the week. The monthly picture looks equally discouraging, with gold shedding approximately 6.5% to 7% over 30 days and roughly 7.5% to 8.5% since the beginning of 2026.

Gold prices have retreated approximately 26% from their late-January peak near $5,400 to $5,600, pressured by elevated Treasury yields, higher oil prices and expectations of prolonged restrictive Federal Reserve policy. Despite the recent selling, gold remains more than 120% higher over five years. Meanwhile, the World Gold Council estimates above-ground stocks at approximately 222,600 tonnes, representing roughly 60 years of current annual mine production.

Global mining output reached approximately 3,672 tonnes in 2025. Matching that annual supply through Marathon’s proposed process would require approximately 1,800 gigawatts of thermal fusion capacity, assuming its theoretical yields hold.

Commercial fusion plants don’t yet operate at that scale, and the economics of synthetic gold remain unproven. Even if the process eventually becomes commercially viable, the resulting metal would be chemically indistinguishable from naturally mined gold.

Bitcoiners Troll Gold Bugs Over Marathon Fusion’s Breakthrough

Bitcoin proponents, meanwhile, have seized on Marathon’s announcement to needle longtime gold advocates, arguing that the ability to manufacture gold exposes a fundamental weakness in the precious metal’s scarcity narrative. Some have drawn comparisons to laboratory-grown diamonds, while others have joked about funding fusion research to undermine gold’s monetary premium. Real, earth-crafted diamonds have seen a 50% drop in value since the introduction of lab diamonds.

The argument has also revived the familiar rivalry between bitcoin supporters and gold advocate Peter Schiff, with Bitcoiners pointing to the network’s 21 million coin supply limit as a distinction. Gold defenders counter that theoretical production and economically viable manufacturing are entirely different propositions, leaving the age-old debate over which asset represents harder money far from settled.

For now, gold’s immediate challenge comes from financial markets, not nuclear alchemy. The real question is whether manufacturing a marketable ounce will ever cost less than buying one.

title: BCG Study Puts Custody At The Center Of Banks’ Digital Asset Plans
summary: New BCG research examines how custody controls, technology choices and integration affect banks’ plans for digital asset services.
content:
TL;DR: A BCG study commissioned by Ripple argues that banks’ custody choices shape the digital asset services they can offer. Its modeled earnings opportunity is an illustration, while the report’s adoption estimate excludes assets on centralized exchanges.

For a bank planning to move into digital assets, the custody decision can determine which products it is able to build.

That is the argument in research announced by Boston Consulting Group on October 22. The study, commissioned by Ripple, estimates that more than 30% of digital assets outside centralized exchanges are held through institutional custody models.

The exclusion matters: the figure is not a claim that institutions hold 30% of the entire crypto market through third-party custodians. BCG’s category also includes enterprise self-custody and wallet-as-a-service arrangements, which involve different degrees of control and outsourcing.

The Choice Goes Beyond Who Holds The Keys

BCG identifies several custody models and argues that banks may need a combination, depending on the services they intend to offer. The research emphasizes governance, integration and the ability to work across providers.

In Ripple’s account of the findings, large banks are increasingly licensing self-custody technology and building client products on top, while wallet-as-a-service is gaining traction among payment and retail fintechs. The company also highlights demand for common controls across multiple custodians.

That helps explain why custody is a product-design decision as well as a security decision. Holding assets for long periods is a different workflow from moving collateral between venues or settling a stream of payments. The same key-management technology can support either, but approval policies and operational processes will differ.

Consider a bank using a stablecoin for payments. A secure signing system still needs to establish who is allowed to instruct a payment, how limits apply and what happens when instructions conflict. Security at the cryptographic level cannot, by itself, answer those business questions.

A Business-Case Estimate With Clear Limits

BCG’s illustrative analysis suggests a regional bank with $200 billion to $300 billion in assets could generate $80 million to $100 million in profit-and-loss upside by combining custody choices with five digital asset use cases. That is a modeled opportunity, not reported earnings or a forecast that every comparable bank will achieve it.

The sponsorship also belongs in the picture. Ripple sells custody infrastructure and commissioned the work. The report can offer a useful framework while still reflecting a commercial interest in expanding the market.

There is an established supervisory backdrop. In a July 2025 joint statement, US banking regulators reminded banks that crypto safekeeping must meet existing safety, soundness and legal requirements. They said the statement created no new supervisory expectations.

For banks considering tokenized assets, the practical question is therefore which controls, integrations and liabilities accompany the proposed revenue. The strongest business case would show how a specific service earns money after its operating costs and risks, rather than relying on an industry-wide adoption number.

Written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

title: Grayscale Tracks 580% Crypto Winner Targeting AI Computing Revenue
summary: Grayscale is highlighting three crypto projects addressing artificial intelligence (AI) training data, hardware financing, and computing revenue. PEARL’s reported 580% three-month gain accompanies the firm’s assessment of blockchain applications across the industry’s supply chain. PEARL’s 580% Gain ...
content:
Grayscale is highlighting three crypto projects addressing artificial intelligence (AI) training data, hardware financing, and computing revenue. PEARL’s reported 580% three-month gain accompanies the firm’s assessment of blockchain applications across the industry’s supply chain.

Key Takeaways

  • Grayscale reports PEARL gained 580% over three months through Oct. 22.
  • DATA aims to turn human-contributed training material into paid datasets.
  • USD.AI channels blockchain capital into loans secured by computing hardware.

PEARL’s 580% Gain Puts AI Computing Rewards in Focus

Blockchain projects are developing ways to earn revenue from AI infrastructure, with PEARL among three examples highlighted by Grayscale on Oct. 23. Zach Pandl, head of research at the digital asset manager, examined PEARL, DATA Network, and USD.AI as examples of blockchain applications in AI infrastructure.

Pearl, a blockchain project focused on AI computing, aims to let graphics processing units (GPUs) perform AI tasks while simultaneously securing a proof-of-work blockchain. These chips perform many calculations in parallel. Operators could earn blockchain rewards alongside payments for AI services.

The analysis reported PEARL’s 580% gain over three months, citing Coingecko data through Oct. 22. Pandl qualified the projects’ prospects:

“Their long-term relevance will depend on adoption and competitive economics.”

DATA Targets Paid Contributions to AI Training

Human-contributed photographs, videos, and voice recordings form the basis of DATA Network’s approach to supplying material for AI development. The project is building collection, licensing, and tracking tools. Applications using its infrastructure could license datasets to AI laboratories while rewarding the individuals who supplied the information.

Training data is material that models process to learn patterns, making its quality and variety relevant to their capabilities. DATA announced plans Oct. 12 to move its protocol, the software and rules governing its operations, to the Sui blockchain and use Walrus, a decentralized file-storage network, as its default storage layer.

USD.AI Connects Blockchain Funding With GPU Loans

Expensive computing equipment creates financing needs that USD.AI, a blockchain-based lending platform, addresses through loans secured by GPUs and their associated cash flows. Its GPU financing terms describe funding of up to 80% of deployment costs, subject to credit review and eligibility. Borrowers contribute at least 20% of the cost themselves and repay principal over three to five years.

Pooled capital can fund those loans and potentially generate returns for participants. More broadly, decentralized finance lending uses blockchain software to administer financial transactions. Participants remain exposed to borrower defaults, collateral losses, and software failures.

Institutional backing for this approach includes crypto exchange Bullish’s (NYSE: BLSH) $100 million credit facility for USD.AI, announced in August to finance GPU-backed loans. That arrangement connects stablecoin capital with physical equipment supporting AI services.

Hardware financing also underpins a $43 million hardware and financing agreement between Vertical Data and Alpha Compute Corp. (Nasdaq: ALP), then named Alphaton Capital. The April deal covered infrastructure using Nvidia’s B300, a chip model designed for AI workloads, and operational services for privacy-preserving computing.

Nvidia’s (Nasdaq: NVDA) proposed partnerships with six financial institutions target more than $500 billion for AI infrastructure over time. Announced Aug. 10 and subject to final agreements, those platforms would leave financing decisions to institutions assessing customer demand, cash flow, utilization, and residual equipment value.

title: Kraken Parent Payward Wins In-Principle Approval For Kazakhstan Expansion
summary: Payward’s Kazakhstan plan moves forward with preliminary approval for trading and custody, while full licensing remains a separate step.
content:
TL;DR: Payward has received in-principle approval for a Kazakhstan business covering digital asset trading, dealing and custody in the AIFC. Final licensing conditions remain relevant, and the announcement gives no customer launch date.

Kraken parent Payward has moved closer to establishing a regulated business in Kazakhstan, with preliminary approval for several activities rather than trading alone.

In an October 22 announcement, Payward said the Astana Financial Services Authority had granted in-principle approval to license Payward Kazakhstan in the Astana International Financial Centre. The proposed permissions cover operating a digital asset trading facility, dealing in investments as principal and agent, and digital asset custody.

The company also said Kazakh traders would gain access to its global order books. It did not give a date for the local service to open. For prospective local customers, the distinction between that plan and a completed launch is the most immediate detail.

The License Still Has A Final Stage

AFSA’s authorization guide explains that in-principle approval sets out conditions and recommendations an applicant must satisfy before receiving its license. The process can involve establishing a legal entity, injecting capital and resolving other regulatory matters.

The guide also says applicants must demonstrate sufficient financial and human resources, systems and internal controls for the activities they propose. Those are general licensing requirements; Payward’s brief announcement does not disclose the particular conditions attached to its own approval.

That makes the announcement evidence of progress through the licensing process. It is not evidence that every planned product is already available or that the same permissions apply outside the AIFC. Customers ultimately need to know which local entity provides a service and exactly what that entity is licensed to do.

Local Permissions, A Global Order Book

The proposed combination is commercially significant because an exchange serves more than one function. Trading brings buyers and sellers together; dealing permissions concern how the firm participates in transactions; custody concerns responsibility for customers’ assets.

Those functions can sit behind a single app, but their risks differ. A competitive execution price says little about the handling of a withdrawal dispute, just as a strong custody arrangement does not guarantee a deep trading market.

Access to wider order books could be useful if the eventual service connects local demand with more counterparties. That potential benefit should be assessed through actual execution quality, fees and withdrawal arrangements once services are available. The announcement alone cannot establish those outcomes.

For traders considering Bitcoin or other digital assets through the planned operation, the next concrete milestone is the final license and a clear description of the products, eligible customers and opening date. The preliminary approval advances that process while leaving those practical questions to the next stage.

Written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

title: Keystone Wallet Data Breach Exposes Buyers’ Addresses to Scammers
summary: Hardware wallet maker Keystone disclosed a customer data breach on Saturday, after unauthorized access to its website exposed names, shipping addresses, contact information and purchase details. The company says recovery phrases and private keys remain secure. The incident adds Keystone to a growing...
content:
Hardware wallet maker Keystone disclosed a customer data breach on Saturday, after unauthorized access to its website exposed names, shipping addresses, contact information and purchase details. The company says recovery phrases and private keys remain secure. The incident adds Keystone to a growing list of hardware wallet manufacturers facing security problems in 2026, including Ledger, Trezor, Safepal and Coldcard.

Key Takeaways

  • Keystone disclosed an Oct. 24 breach exposing customer shipping information and purchase details.
  • Keystone says private keys, recovery phrases and payment information were not compromised.
  • Coldcard, Ledger, Trezor and Safepal also faced major security incidents in 2026.

Keystone Customer Data Breach Exposes Buyers to Targeted Scams

A hardware wallet designed to keep cryptocurrency secrets offline has encountered a security problem somewhere entirely different: its online storefront. On Saturday, Keystone disclosed at 1:59 p.m. ET that an unauthorized party had obtained customer shipping information through its website, potentially giving scammers the personal details needed to impersonate the company.

Keystone insists that recovery phrases, private keys and payment information were not compromised, but the incident raises an uncomfortable question about how much protection an offline wallet provides when its owner’s identity and address are exposed.

Keystone Confirms Unauthorized Access

Keystone disclosed on X that it detected suspicious access Oct. 20 and subsequently examined application programming interface (API) activity with Shopify, its e-commerce provider. By Oct. 23, the company had confirmed that an unauthorized third party obtained customer names, contact information, shipping addresses, and purchase details.

The company says it blocked the intrusion, patched the vulnerability, and began notifying affected customers. However, Keystone has not disclosed how many buyers were exposed or precisely how the unauthorized access occurred.

Scammers Gain a Potential Opening

The immediate danger isn’t necessarily someone remotely emptying a hardware wallet. It’s someone using legitimate customer information to manufacture a convincing deception. Keystone warned customers about fraudulent refund offers, replacement devices, and unsolicited messages requesting sensitive information. The company emphasized that it never requests recovery phrases or private keys.

One X user wrote about the issue the day before Keystone confirmed the attack. “Just raising awareness here because I’m 99% convinced your customer database may have been leaked. I received a call from a spoofed Montreal SPVM number, and the guy tried to social-engineer me,” the X account OG Degen wrote. Customers should independently verify communications through Keystone’s official website rather than following unexpected links.

Hardware Wallet Security Takes Another Hit in 2026

Keystone’s disclosure follows a difficult year for hardware wallet manufacturers. Coldcard faced a massive bug with weak seed-generation randomness and substantial estimated losses, while Ledger confronted reports of tampered devices distributed through a reseller.

Trezor and Safepal also disclosed customer information breaches involving third-party fulfillment or ordering systems. Unlike incidents involving compromised recovery phrases, those exposures primarily created opportunities for phishing and impersonation.

For Keystone, the cryptographic defenses reportedly held. The troubling question is whether customers’ personal information received comparable protection.

title: FCA Proposes Crypto Crime Guidance On Wallet Checks And Blockchain Analytics
summary: The FCA’s Financial Crime Guide consultation sets out proposed examples of good and poor practice as crypto firms prepare for wider supervision.
content:
TL;DR: The FCA is consulting on updated financial crime guidance for crypto businesses, including customer checks, blockchain analytics and the Travel Rule. Responses are due December 24, and the guide itself would not create new rules.

Crypto businesses preparing for the UK’s expanded regulatory regime have a more detailed picture of the controls the Financial Conduct Authority expects them to build.

The regulator’s October 23 consultation proposes changes to its Financial Crime Guide, covering cryptoassets alongside fraud, sanctions, data security and money laundering. The proposals apply to the FCA’s financial crime supervisory population, including cryptoasset businesses and firms overseen under the Money Laundering Regulations.

The practical focus is on how firms assess customers and transactions, and how they react when risk changes. A blockchain record can help an investigation, but a record alone does not decide whether a customer explanation is credible or a transfer needs further scrutiny.

Analytics Must Sit Inside A Working Control System

The consultation paper proposes examples of good and poor practice for enhanced due diligence, onboarding and transaction monitoring. It specifically addresses the use of blockchain analytics and further guidance on the Travel Rule, which concerns information accompanying certain transfers.

The paper also reminds firms that governance must evolve as their businesses grow. Its proposed changes include a question about whether policies and staff training distinguish obligations under proceeds-of-crime legislation from those under terrorism legislation.

For an exchange or provider of custody, the implication is that buying a screening product is only one part of the job. Someone still has to set its thresholds, review alerts and document decisions. A technically accurate warning is of limited use if it sits unreviewed while funds move elsewhere.

That matters for stablecoin transfers as much as for volatile tokens. A stable unit price does not establish the identity of a sender or the origin of funds. Transaction risk and market risk are different questions, and control systems need to reflect that distinction.

Guidance Now, A Wider Regime In 2027

The FCA says the guide contains no rules and imposes no new requirements. It is intended to help firms understand supervisory expectations and assess their own arrangements. The consultation closes on December 24, after which the regulator plans to publish feedback and the final text in a policy statement.

Separately, the FCA’s regime overview says the wider cryptoasset framework is expected to begin on October 25, 2027. Applications for authorization are already open, and the regulator published a package of final rules in June.

The distinction between those stages matters for firms planning investment in compliance. This consultation does not postpone existing anti-money-laundering duties until next year, nor does it bring the whole future regime into force immediately. It fills in the proposed guidance firms can use when translating their obligations into day-to-day decisions.

Written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

title: Silver Price Analysis as October Sell-Off Tests the Market’s Recovery Prospects
summary: Traders are looking to test the lows as the momentum slows and major support levels present themselves, and then whether the selling pressure will persist or turn to a rally before the end of December.
content:
Skip to content
Assets: XAG

Traders are looking to test the lows as the momentum slows and major support levels present themselves, and then whether the selling pressure will persist or turn to a rally before the end of December.

The swift drop in silver prices in October has put the precious metal at a pivotal level, and the metal has dropped by almost 6% over the last week.

Silver Extends Its October Decline as Selling Pressure Builds

The supplied Trading Economics chart shows silver prices dropping 5.96% for the week to $53.883 per ounce.The weekly chang show-3.412. The prices were again hovering around $53.9 on October 24, and the chart was indicating a big pullback from above $57 earlier this week.

The drop further escalated since October 22, when silver breached the $56 level and headed down to $54. Source: TradingEconomics

The price closed in the mid-$50s, before stabilising a fraction of a penny higher. The chart displays a brief period of consolidation late in the week; however, this is not yet a confirmation of a longer-term reversal.

Further market commentary also highlights yield pressures, a stronger US dollar and interest-rate expectations. On October 23, FOREX.com news agency said that silver had found a long-term support base of 50-55 after a wide precious-metals sell-off.

TradingView Signals Point to a Weak Technical Structure

As of October 24, silver was trading at $53.918 on the provided TradingView chart, which had declined by 1.26% during the session. The displayed moving averages were at $61.309 and $63.618, respectively, which were still above the price. Both were on a downward trend, suggesting that prices in recent times have been subdued during the considered time periods.

The Relative Strength Index (RSI) was at 31.58, which is below the average level of 38.21. The latest reading puts silver near the 30 level, which is typically seen as oversold. Source: TradingView

But this isn’t a conclusive sign of recovery, especially if the prices continue in the form of lower lows. The first important area of the technical zone is the interval between $53 and $55. Any continuation of the trend below $53 would leave the market open for more losses to the $50 price level.

On the other hand, a recovery above $55 will signal an initial stabilisation. However, with more evidence of a change in trend, silver would need to reach higher levels and test resistance at $61-$64.

These levels are technical levels that you are given in this chart and NOT guaranteed future trading levels. A change in the price action may be in sight, depending on the direction of US Treasury yields, the dollar and the general sentiment on precious metals.

October and December Forecasts rely on a Market Reversal.

October and December Forecasts Depend on a Market Reversal

However, the charts are looking for caution for the rest of the month as silver is still trading below its period averages. A break above $55 would signal a short-term recovery, while a drop below $53 would increase downside risk. The 50-55 zone continues to be significant as market analysts have found it to be a wider support area.

December is a more ambiguous month. In the August forecast, J.P. Morgan had an average of $63/oz. for Q4 and $70.60/oz. for 2026. The forecast aligned with expectations of easing physical-market tightness, declining industrial demand, and interest-rate pressures. These are average which are forecasts and do not guarantee December closing prices.

On X, Rashad Hajiyev stated that silver has formed a long-term cup and handle breakout and retest. Prices may even reach $200 by 2027, he said. Source: X Via Rashad

This, of course, is an analyst’s bull case and not a market consensus or actual projection. Buyers would have needed to take control and break out of the technical resistance near $60–$63 to make a move in December.

A continued lacklustre performance may instead drag silver down to around $50–$55. The evidence provided herein suggests that the next few months are a period of caution until prices recover and cross key moving averages, but the longer-term trend depends on monetary policy, industrial demand and investment flows.

title: X 100 Global Loses Millions as Three-Seat Senate Is Hijacked
summary: Several reports say X 100 Global suffered a devastating governance takeover on Saturday, after attackers reportedly captured two of its three Senate seats and exploited their majority to raid the project’s treasury. Blockaid traced approximately $4.85 million in USDT proceeds and additional token wi...
content:
Several reports say X 100 Global suffered a devastating governance takeover on Saturday, after attackers reportedly captured two of its three Senate seats and exploited their majority to raid the project’s treasury. Blockaid traced approximately $4.85 million in USDT proceeds and additional token withdrawals. The X token plunged more than 96%, while liquidity evaporated across decentralized trading pools.

Key Takeaways

  • Attackers reportedly seized two of X 100 Global’s three Senate seats through a flash-loan exploit.
  • Blockaid traced approximately $4.85 million in USDT proceeds from the X 100 Global attack.
  • X 100 Global’s token reportedly crashed more than 96% as Uniswap liquidity disappeared.

X 100 Global Governance Attack Drains Millions as Token Crashes 96%

Another day, another hack in 2026. According to a myriad of onchain security alerts, the cryptocurrency project built around a three-seat governing Senate discovered just how dangerous instant democracy can become when attackers reportedly bought their way into two seats and promptly emptied millions from its treasury.

X 100 Global, an Ethereum-based project, suffered a unique governance takeover on Oct. 24 that security firm Blockaid traced to a flash-loan operation extracting approximately $4.85 million in USDT. Its X token subsequently collapsed more than 96%, leaving holders facing a market with virtually no liquidity.

Attackers Bought Control and Emptied the Treasury

The exploit targeted X 100 Global’s governance architecture rather than exploiting a conventional smart-contract coding error. Security firm Exvul explained the root cause in full detail. Attackers reportedly borrowed approximately 1.94 million USDT through an Aave flash loan, purchased X tokens and registered helper contracts to occupy two of the project’s three Senate seats.

Here’s the catch: Governance lacked voting snapshots, minimum holding periods and execution delays. That allowed the attackers to acquire voting power, approve malicious proposals and execute transactions almost immediately.

One transaction transferred 400,000 X tokens from the project’s Freezer treasury into an attacker-controlled liquidity pool, returning approximately 36 USDT to the treasury. The attackers subsequently extracted those tokens and sold them through a legitimate Uniswap V3 pool.

$4.85 Million Extracted as Liquidity Disappears

Blockaid, Exvul and several other onchain security teams and investigators reported transaction analysis identified approximately $4.85 million in USDT proceeds alongside roughly 550,000 X tokens extracted across three transactions. Subsequent operations targeted additional Uniswap V3 liquidity positions.

The market consequences were severe. X plunged from the $50-60 range to approximately $1.75, a decline exceeding 96%. Decentralized exchanged (DEX) trading data on Saturday showed certain liquidity measurements falling to just a few dollars, leaving meaningful sell orders vulnerable to extraordinary slippage.

Approximately 12.2 million X tokens reportedly remained in the Freezer during Blockaid’s latest cited update, when the incident was still described as ongoing. No immediate official project statement has been released at the time of writing (3 p.m. EST on 10/24). The central vulnerability was strikingly simple: A treasury governed by three seats apparently allowed outsiders to purchase a controlling majority and execute its decisions without waiting.

The incident remains ongoing, and X 100 Global has yet to acknowledge the breach or issue a statement through its social media channels. This article will be updated if additional details come to light.

title: New York Seeks $1.3 Billion From NovaTech Founders In Crypto Fraud Case
summary: A new court filing seeks monetary relief from NovaTech’s founders after an earlier default judgment, alongside settlements with promoters.
content:
TL;DR: New York’s attorney general is seeking $1.3 billion in monetary relief in the NovaTech case and has announced nearly $6 million in promoter settlements. The larger sum is a request to the court, not money recovered for investors.

New York’s effort to recover losses from the NovaTech cryptocurrency scheme has reached a new stage, with Attorney General Letitia James asking a court to impose roughly $1.3 billion in damages and disgorgement.

The October 22 announcement also disclosed nearly $6 million in settlements with four promoters. Those are separate from the much larger claim involving founders Cynthia and Eddy Petion. The announcement does not establish that either amount has already reached victims.

The case concerns investment packages sold through NovaTech and an earlier business, AWS Mining. According to the attorney general, the schemes targeted Haitian and other immigrant communities through religious networks, social media and messaging groups.

The New Filing Follows An Earlier Judgment

An affirmation filed on October 22 supports the request for monetary relief. It records that New York sued in June 2024 and that the defaulting defendants did not respond or appear. The court entered a default order and judgment on August 4, 2025.

The latest motion asks the court to determine the financial consequences. It should not be confused with a new criminal conviction, a completed recovery or a guarantee that a judgment can be collected. Those distinctions are particularly important when the sums sought are much larger than the settlements announced alongside them.

The promoter figures listed by the attorney general are $2.9 million from Martin Zizi, $2.05 million from Frantz Ciceron, $750,000 from James Corbett and $275,861 from Ricardo Roy Sr. All four face permanent bans from the securities, commodities and cryptocurrency industries.

The timing also needs care: the Zizi consent papers were filed in November 2025. This week’s announcement brings the settlement figures together; it does not mean every agreement was signed this week.

Recruitment Promises Outran The Trading Business

The original mining operation offered high returns and recruiting bonuses, according to the court affirmation. NovaTech later marketed cryptocurrency trading packages. The cryptocurrency label described how investors supplied money, but the underlying issue was what operators actually did with it.

That is a useful distinction for readers assessing similar pitches. An account balance on a website does not establish that assets exist, that trades occurred or that withdrawals can be honored. Nor does a familiar community connection answer questions about custody and control of funds.

For affected investors, the next substantive development will be the court’s decision on monetary relief and any subsequent recovery process. The announced settlements and the requested award address different defendants and different steps in that process; combining them into a headline recovery figure would overstate what has happened.

Related reading: How crypto exchanges work.

Written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

title: Bitcoin Price Sinks to $79,146 as Liquidations Rock Weekend Trading
summary: Bitcoin’s price cracked below $80,000 on Saturday, touching its lowest price in more than a month as leveraged traders absorbed hundreds of millions in liquidations. The weekend selloff handed longtime bitcoin critic Peter Schiff fresh ammunition for an even darker prediction. Bitcoin’s $80,000 Floo...
content:
Bitcoin’s price cracked below $80,000 on Saturday, touching its lowest price in more than a month as leveraged traders absorbed hundreds of millions in liquidations. The weekend selloff handed longtime bitcoin critic Peter Schiff fresh ammunition for an even darker prediction.

Key Takeaways

  • Bitcoin’s price fell to approximately $79,146 Saturday as leveraged liquidations accelerated the selloff.
  • Peter Schiff predicts bitcoin will test $75,000 and warns ETF investors face a difficult weekend.
  • Blackrock and Fidelity led a reported $635.6 million exodus from U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs this week.

Bitcoin’s $80,000 Floor Gives Way as Liquidations Mount

Bitcoin’s price slipped to approximately $79,146 on Oct. 24, marking its second sharp test of the $80,000 threshold in roughly 10 days. By early afternoon, the cryptocurrency traded between $79,400, $79,700, and back above $80,000 again, down approximately 2.3% to 2.5% over 24 hours.

The selling caught leveraged traders flat-footed. More than $810 million in cryptocurrency positions reportedly vanished within the last day, including approximately $689 million in bullish bets. Broader 24-hour liquidations show more than 200,000 traders wiped out, according to Coinglass.com stats. Thin weekend liquidity compounded the pressure. Once bitcoin breached $80,000, forced liquidations accelerated selling into an already weakened market.

Peter Schiff Targets $75,000 as ETF Investors Face Weekend Lockout

Gold advocate and longtime bitcoin critic Peter Schiff wasted little time weighing in, stating:

“Bitcoin is finally breaking down. It’s hard to believe it’s held up this long. Now that it’s below $80K, the next stop is likely $75K. If that level fails to hold today, it’s going to be a very long weekend for Bitcoiners, especially for ETF investors who can’t sell until Monday.”

Schiff’s warning points to an important distinction. Bitcoin trades continuously, but U.S.-listed spot bitcoin exchange-traded funds (ETFs) generally cannot be traded on stock exchanges during weekends. Investors holding those shares must wait until Monday’s session to react.

Institutional demand had already weakened. U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs lost $635.6 million earlier this week, led by approximately $254 million from Blackrock’s IBIT and $217.5 million from Fidelity’s FBTC. Another $138 million reportedly exited Oct. 23.

Technical Breakdown Meets Oil Shock and Fed Uncertainty

Bitcoin also slipped beneath its 50-day simple moving average near $81,700 to $81,800, breaking a technical support level that had held for approximately two months. Traders are now watching support around $78,400 and $77,876, followed by a broader zone between $76,700 and $72,500.

Beyond crypto, technology-stock weakness and elevated oil prices have complicated the outlook. Brent crude is coasting along above $117 on Saturday amid Middle East tensions, adding inflation concerns ahead of the Federal Reserve’s Oct. 27-28 meeting.

The immediate question isn’t whether Schiff gets his $75,000 target. It’s whether bitcoin buyers can reclaim $80,000 before ETF investors return on Monday.

title: SEC Puts Tokenization On Its 2027 Examination Agenda
summary: The SEC’s new examination agenda puts tokenized securities, clearing infrastructure and technology controls under the spotlight.
content:
TL;DR: The SEC has named tokenization among its fiscal 2027 examination priorities, bringing the systems behind blockchain securities into closer supervisory focus. The staff document sets inspection priorities and creates no new legal obligations.

The SEC’s tokenization agenda now includes a practical question for financial firms: can the infrastructure work reliably when something goes wrong?

In its October 23 announcement, the US regulator placed tokenization among the market developments its examiners will scrutinize during fiscal 2027. The wider program also covers investment advice, complex products, private credit and cybersecurity across more than 34,000 registrants.

For companies building services around tokenized assets, that brings the discussion down from the promise of faster trading to the controls supporting it. A share recorded on a blockchain still needs dependable ownership records, functioning markets and an orderly response to disruption.

Clearing And Trading Systems Enter The Frame

The 20-page examination document explicitly includes tokenization among high-risk areas for clearing-agency reviews. In its discussion of Regulation Systems Compliance and Integrity, it lists tokenized securities alongside extended trading hours, advanced AI and quantum computing. Cloud providers and other technology suppliers also feature in those reviews.

That combination matters. Extending trading hours can leave less time for maintenance, while connecting a token to conventional securities records adds another place where systems must agree. The relevant test is whether the complete service remains dependable, including the handoffs between systems.

The document separately emphasizes cybersecurity governance, access controls, incident response and risks from shared technology. It also states that the priorities are staff views, carry no legal force and do not amend existing law. An examination focus should therefore be read as a signal about supervision, rather than a new tokenization license or prohibition.

A Permission To Experiment Still Comes With Conditions

The context is the SEC’s September innovation exemption for certain tokenized stock venues. That temporary framework requires equivalent shareholder rights, issuer notification and an opportunity to object when an unaffiliated party tokenizes shares. It also imposes trading limits and requirements for public, auditable smart contracts.

Those conditions illustrate why market access and operational supervision move together. A permitted venue can still have weak controls; a technically impressive platform can still mishandle an investor’s rights. The new priorities put attention on that gap.

For investors, the useful distinction is between the token and the service built around it. Questions about who holds the underlying security, how transactions reconcile and what happens during an outage remain relevant alongside the blockchain’s design. Custody and market infrastructure do not become incidental simply because a trade uses a token.

The SEC says its priorities are non-exhaustive and may change during the year. Tokenization’s place in the published agenda nevertheless gives firms a clear reason to expect scrutiny of how their systems operate, as well as what their products promise.

Written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

title: Strategy, Strive face balancing act between bitcoin buying and preferred stock dividends
summary: The securities have financed purchases of nearly 136,000 bitcoin, opening a funding channel that analysts expect to complement the larger ETF market.
content:
Oct 24, 2026, 12:00 p.m. EDT

3 min read

Summary

  • Since 2025, preferred stocks funded purchases of 135,979 BTC through Oct. 5, Fidelity said.
  • Bitwise expects ETFs to remain the larger demand source, with preferreds attracting yield investors.
  • Dividend obligations and buybacks could constrain further bitcoin purchases.

Bitcoin BTC$84,459.46 treasury companies like Strategy (MSTR) and Strive (ASST), whose purchases help maintain demand for the largest cryptocurrency, have a tough balancing act, according to Fidelity Digital Assets and analysts who spoke to CoinDesk.

On the one hand, they need cash to fund their purchases. On the other, they need to maintain investor appetite for new sales of the perpetual preferred stock that is their favored fundraising vehicle. As the number of shares in circulation grows, so do the dividend payments.

The securities, which sit between debt and common equity in the capital structure with regular payouts and no voting rights, have financed purchases of some 136,000 bitcoin in the 20 months since their introduction, Fidelity research analyst Zack Wainwright wrote in a Tuesday report. That’s more than 0.5% of the cryptocurrency’s maximum supply.

Strategy, the largest corporate bitcoin holder, is the dominant company in the market. Its preferred shares — it has five different classes — make it a bellwether for the model’s durability. Its first offering, STRK, debuted in February 2025.

Fidelity puts the bitcoin-focused preferred market at roughly $12 billion. The global fixed-income market is $150 trillion, suggesting there’s room for growth.

Reaching yield investors

By selling preferred shares that offer dividends without a fixed maturity, the companies reduce refinancing pressure while attracting investors reluctant to own bitcoin directly.

“Perpetual preferreds have brought bitcoin to income investors, a group that ETFs never reached,” said Mark Palmer, a senior equity research analyst at StoneX.

Ryan Rasmussen, the head of research at Bitwise, also sees the products attracting buyers who might avoid bitcoin exchange-traded funds, though he expects the ETFs to remain the bigger demand channel.

“Over the long run, I expect ETFs to be a larger source of demand for bitcoin, with perpetual preferred offerings acting as a second tailwind addressing a different type of investor (yield investors),” Rasmussen said.

James Butterfill, CoinShares’ head of research, said STRC alone, which pays a variable dividend currently around 12%, raised $7.5 billion during 2026 through late July. That funding carries a recurring dividend cost.

Alex Blume, the founder and CEO of institutional bitcoin asset manager Two Prime, pointed out that products such as STRC and Strive’s SATA don’t offer just exposure to bitcoin prices. Their price also reacts to management competence, issuers’ obligations and capital-market conditions.

He cited STRC briefly falling into the $70 range in late June as evidence of potential volatility. Growing issuance creates a tension between increasing bitcoin per common share, meeting dollar-denominated dividend-payout commitments and avoiding bitcoin sales, he said. The Strategy preferred stock currently trades around $99.40.

Buybacks compete with purchases

“The catch is that the demand for perpetual preferreds is reflexive,” Palmer said. Continued preferred-funded buying depends on the securities trading at or near par, he added. Below par, fresh issuance becomes less attractive, and companies may favor repurchases, Butterfill said.

Strategy’s latest weekly update reported $193 million spent repurchasing STRC alongside purchases of just 267 bitcoin, according to Butterfill. The firm also increased its preferred-stock repurchase authorization to $3 billion, he said.

“Buybacks can reduce future dividend costs, but they compete with bitcoin purchases for capital today,” Butterfill said.

Cash reserves provide a buffer, although Strategy has already sold some bitcoin to fund preferred dividends, he added.

ETFs remain the larger channel

U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs have attracted approximately $57 billion in cumulative net inflows and hold around $106 billion in assets, Butterfill said.

Net ETF creations increase funds’ bitcoin holdings, while issuance of preferred stock gives management discretion over spending. Redemptions can reverse ETF demand but leave no continuing dividend commitment, he said.

Butterfill sees preferreds amplifying the cycle: supporting purchases when financing conditions are favorable, with that support weakening as sentiment deteriorates.
