title: Bitcoin ETFs Lose Over $635M In One Day Following Oil Price Spike
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

Bitcoin ETFs Lose Over $635M In One Day Following Oil Price Spike 
Investors this week were buying bitcoin ETFs but that all changed on Thursday. 
This post Bitcoin ETFs Lose Over $635M In One Day Following Oil Price Spike  first appeared on Bitcoin Magazine and is written by Mathe...
content:
U.S. investors quickly reversed course on Thursday, cashing out over half a billion dollars from spot bitcoin exchange-traded funds as risk-off sentiment surfaced again. 

A total of $635.6 million left the funds on Thursday, data from Farside Investors shows. The redemptions put downward pressure on the price of bitcoin, which dropped under $81,000 at one point. 

The coin has since rebounded and was recently trading for nearly $81,669, down just 1% over a 24-hour period. 

BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust saw the biggest outflows, with investors cashing out over $254 million. Fidelity’s Wise Origin Bitcoin Fund followed, losing close to $218 million. 

Over $109 million left the ARK 21Shares Bitcoin ETF; Morgan Stanley’s fund and Bitwise’s ETF lost nearly $30 million and over $27 million, respectively. 

But the investment vehicles this week have this week received net positive investment of over $439 million. 

Investors went into “risk-off” mode after flare ups in the Middle East sent the price of oil higher. Brent crude hit its highest price in five months after Yemeni rebel group the Houthis on Thursday attacked Saudi Arabia, sparking concerns over more disruption to energy supplies. 

Bitcoin’s price has been rattled this year since the U.S. and Israel attacked Iran, halting oil supplies as ships have struggled to pass through the strategic Strait of Hormuz, where a fifth of the world’s oil passes through. 

A higher oil price can hurt the price of bitcoin and other “risk-on” assets because it increases the chances of the U.S. central bank raising interest rates. 

Bitcoin has typically done well in a low interest rate environment because it means the asset has more liquidity to rally. 

Investors on Thursday also sold off tech stocks, which had rallied earlier in the week off the back of SpaceX’s impressive earnings. 

Analysts are saying bitcoin is entering a bull market again. Data last month showed that  the leading cryptocurrency crossed above its 365-day moving average — a typical sign it is out of a bear market — following a strong run in August. 

Bitcoin notched a record of $126,080 in October 2025 but then began to sink later that month after the biggest liquidation event in crypto history saw over $19 billion in bets closed. 

The coin spent the first half of 2026 trading well below that level but picked up again in August and September, having its best quarter in years. 

Mathew Di Salvo

Mathew is a reporter who's covered the space since 2019, reporting on everything from Salvadoran president Nayib Bukele's Bitcoin bet to crypto exchange FTX's bankruptcy.

title: OpenAI Cuts $150 Billion Valuation as Anthropic Reports $80 Billion Loss: Is the AI Boom Cracking?
summary: OpenAI has reportedly lowered its proposed valuation by $150 billion to $1.25 trillion, while rival Anthropic’s draft IPO prospectus reveals an $80.7 billion first-half net loss, highlighting the financial pressures behind the artificial intelligence boom.
content:
Skip to content

OpenAI has reportedly lowered its proposed valuation by $150 billion to $1.25 trillion, while rival Anthropic’s draft IPO prospectus reveals an $80.7 billion first-half net loss, highlighting the financial pressures behind the artificial intelligence boom.

The developments come as investors scrutinize infrastructure spending, rising computing costs, and the path to profitability. Although both OpenAI and Anthropic continue to attract substantial investor interest, their latest financial disclosures raise questions about whether AI revenue can justify the enormous cost of developing and operating advanced models.

Key Takeaways

  • OpenAI lowered its proposed valuation from $1.4 trillion to $1.25 trillion while seeking approximately $30 billion in fresh funding.
  • Anthropic reported $16.3 billion in first-half 2026 revenue and an $80.7 billion net loss, according to its draft IPO prospectus.
  • Approximately $72 billion of Anthropic’s reported loss came from non-cash accounting adjustments linked to convertible financial instruments.
  • Rising computing expenses, long-term infrastructure commitments, and uncertain returns are increasing scrutiny of AI companies ahead of potential public listings.

OpenAI Valuation Drops $150 Billion: Is the AI Boom in Trouble?

OpenAI has reduced its proposed valuation to $1.25 trillion from $1.4 trillion as negotiations progress on a funding round of approximately $30 billion, according to Bloomberg reporting published on October 23, 2026. The $150 billion adjustment represents a reduction of about 10.7% from its previous target.

OpenAI lowered its valuation target by $150 billion to $1.25 trillion for a proposed $30 billion funding round, with negotiations ongoing. Source: Rohan Paul via X

The revised figure remains well above OpenAI’s March 2026 post-money valuation of $852 billion, established after a reported $122 billion funding round. The new target is approximately 47% higher, indicating that the company’s fundraising ambitions remain substantial despite the adjustment.

The revision does not mean OpenAI has lost $150 billion in realized market value. It reflects a change in the valuation proposed during private fundraising negotiations, which remain ongoing.

The timing is significant. Technology stocks have faced selling pressure following mixed earnings from companies including Meta Platforms and Tesla, intensifying investor concerns that AI infrastructure spending could be growing faster than the returns it generates.

Developing advanced AI systems requires substantial investment in specialized chips, data centers, electricity, and computing capacity. Investors are increasingly assessing whether commercial revenue can grow quickly enough to cover these expenses and support the valuations attached to AI developers.

Why Is OpenAI’s Valuation Falling?

OpenAI’s revised target follows reported investor resistance to its earlier $1.4 trillion valuation, according to the Financial Times. The adjustment may help narrow the gap between the company’s fundraising expectations and investors’ willingness to commit additional capital.

The broader technology selloff has added pressure, as investors reassess the financial returns expected from AI-related investments. However, the available information does not establish that infrastructure spending concerns alone caused OpenAI’s valuation adjustment.

The distinction between a proposed valuation and a completed funding valuation is important. Private-company valuations depend on negotiated financing terms and expectations about future growth, rather than daily market prices. Until the round closes, OpenAI’s $1.25 trillion target remains subject to change.

OpenAI Seeks $30 Billion Ahead of Potential IPO

OpenAI continues to pursue approximately $30 billion in new funding to finance its expansion. Bloomberg reported that Coatue Management was discussing a role as a co-lead investor, while BlackRock and investment funds from the United Arab Emirates were also involved in fundraising discussions.

Bloomberg reports OpenAI has lowered its target valuation to $1.25 trillion for a $30 billion funding round amid investor pushback, down from an initial $1.4 trillion. Source: @business via X

Investor commitments could be finalized by the end of the following week, although the final funding amount and valuation remained uncertain.

The negotiations come as OpenAI prepares for a potential initial public offering in 2027. A public listing would bring greater scrutiny of its financial performance, capital requirements, and progress toward sustainable profitability.

The company faces a balancing act: continuing to invest in model development and computing capacity while demonstrating that its products can generate enough recurring revenue to support those costs. Its reported spending projections of approximately $278 billion in cash through 2030 illustrate the scale of that challenge.

OpenAI’s fundraising outcome could also influence investor expectations for Anthropic, which is preparing for its own potential IPO. Both companies must convince prospective investors that rapid growth can eventually translate into sustainable financial returns.

Anthropic S-1 Shows Red-Hot Growth, Risks, and Massive Computing Costs

Anthropic’s draft IPO prospectus offers another perspective on the financial pressures facing AI developers. According to The Wall Street Journal’s review of the document, the company generated $16.3 billion in revenue during the first half of 2026, up from $1.1 billion in the same period a year earlier.

Anthropic’s draft IPO filing reports $16.3 billion in H1 2026 revenue and an $80.7 billion net loss, largely driven by $72 billion in non-cash valuation charges on convertible instruments. Source: @WSJ via X

Despite that expansion, Anthropic recorded an $80.7 billion net loss, compared with $13 billion a year earlier. Approximately $72 billion of the latest loss came from non-cash accounting charges associated with changes in the estimated value of convertible financial instruments that could become company shares.

Those adjustments do not represent equivalent cash outflows from daily operations. Investors must therefore distinguish the reported net loss from operating expenses and cash-flow performance when assessing Anthropic’s financial health.

Infrastructure costs provide a clearer view of the resources required to operate its business. Anthropic spent nearly $9 billion on computing and infrastructure in the first half of 2026, compared with $2.3 billion a year earlier. The six-month total also exceeded its reported infrastructure spending for all of 2025.

Long-term commitments create additional financial exposure. Reports based on the draft prospectus place Anthropic’s cloud, computing, and infrastructure obligations above $600 billion, with some estimates reaching $750 billion when prospective agreements are included. Much of the spending is tied to contracts that cannot easily be cancelled.

These commitments help secure the capacity needed to meet demand, but they also reduce flexibility if revenue growth slows or computing requirements change.

Growth That Most Companies Never See

Anthropic’s revenue expansion remains substantial. First-half revenue rose from $1.1 billion in 2025 to $16.3 billion in 2026, reflecting growing demand for its AI products and services.

Its Claude Code coding assistant has helped attract developers and enterprise customers seeking tools to support software development and automate technical tasks. This business-focused approach can generate recurring revenue when customers incorporate AI products into their regular workflows.

Anthropic’s third-quarter revenue reportedly increased 45% to $16.8 billion from $11.6 billion in the second quarter. Although the increase remains significant, the sequential growth rate was slower than the more-than-doubling reported between the first and second quarters.

That moderation matters because investors must assess whether revenue can continue expanding fast enough to support rising infrastructure costs. Even a rapidly growing business can face financial pressure if expenses increase at a comparable or faster rate.

Investors have reportedly discussed an Anthropic valuation near $1.5 trillion, below earlier expectations of approximately $2 trillion. The proposed figure would still represent a substantial valuation, placing considerable weight on the company’s ability to maintain growth and improve margins.

The Bill for Being Compute-Starved

Access to computing capacity is a central constraint for advanced AI developers. Training models and operating them at scale require specialized chips, data centers, electricity, and cloud services. Securing sufficient capacity is essential, but competition for those resources can make expansion expensive.

Anthropic’s reported infrastructure commitments reflect the challenge. While estimates of its total obligations vary, the draft prospectus and related reporting point to hundreds of billions of dollars in potential spending over the coming years.

Non-cancellable agreements can provide greater certainty about access to computing resources, but they also create fixed obligations. If demand weakens, Anthropic may be unable to reduce those costs quickly enough to protect its margins.

Its relationships with infrastructure providers add another complication. Amazon, Google, and Microsoft supply cloud services while also developing their own AI products. This overlap creates competing commercial interests and may affect the availability, pricing, and terms of computing agreements.

Anthropic must therefore secure the resources required to serve customers without allowing infrastructure costs to outpace the revenue those resources generate.

Why the Whole Sector Is Watching

Anthropic’s potential IPO could test investor appetite for AI companies that combine rapid revenue growth with significant infrastructure commitments. Its financial disclosures give prospective investors a clearer view of both the commercial opportunity and the costs associated with competing in the sector.

The reception could influence expectations for OpenAI and other AI developers considering public listings. Investors will be watching whether strong revenue growth can support the valuations companies seek, particularly as infrastructure spending absorbs increasing amounts of capital.

OpenAI’s projected cash spending of approximately $278 billion through 2030 underscores the investment required to develop and operate advanced AI systems. The figure also highlights why investors are paying closer attention to capital allocation and the timing of future returns.

Broader technology-market volatility adds uncertainty. If investors become less willing to fund expensive expansion plans, AI companies could face pressure to lower their valuation expectations, reduce spending, or demonstrate a clearer path to profitability.

Is the AI Boom Cracking?

OpenAI’s valuation adjustment and Anthropic’s reported $80.7 billion first-half loss do not establish that the AI boom is ending. OpenAI’s proposed valuation remains above its previous funding benchmark, while Anthropic’s revenue growth demonstrates substantial commercial demand for AI products.

The developments instead highlight a shift in investor priorities. Alongside growth and technical progress, investors increasingly want evidence that AI revenue can cover computing expenses, long-term infrastructure obligations, and the continuing cost of developing advanced models.

OpenAI must secure funding on terms that support its expansion, while Anthropic faces scrutiny of its operating economics and infrastructure commitments ahead of a potential IPO. Both companies will need to show that their business models can support their substantial capital requirements.

The next phase of the AI market may depend less on the amount of capital companies attract and more on how effectively they convert that investment into sustainable earnings and cash flow. The latest disclosures point to greater financial scrutiny, but whether that develops into a broader market correction will depend on actual performance, investor demand, and the industry’s ability to deliver lasting returns.

title: SEC flags tokenization as high-risk area in 2027 market examinations
summary: The SEC’s latest priorities highlight tokenization as an emerging market risk, while cryptocurrencies remain absent as a standalone examination category.
content:
The SEC’s latest priorities highlight tokenization as an emerging market risk, while cryptocurrencies remain absent as a standalone examination category.

The US Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) has added tokenization to its fiscal 2027 examination priorities, placing tokenized securities alongside quantum computing and extended trading hours among emerging trends it plans to examine.

In its 2027 examination priorities, released Friday, the SEC identified tokenization as an area of focus for examinations of critical market infrastructure. Tokenization was not explicitly mentioned in the agency’s 2026 priorities.

The report addressed the security and reliability of critical market infrastructure, stating:

Examinations under Regulation SCI will focus on emerging trends, including SI [super intelligence, the Trump administration’s term for artificial intelligence], tokenization of securities, extended trading hours, and quantum computing.

The SEC also listed tokenization among the high-risk areas it will examine at clearing agencies, alongside default management, securities lending and operational risks.

Cryptocurrencies, meanwhile, remain absent as a standalone examination priority for the second consecutive year. The SEC last included a dedicated section on crypto assets in its fiscal 2025 priorities.

The new priorities come as traditional financial institutions move further into tokenized securities. Earlier this month, an OKX and Intercontinental Exchange joint venture filed to launch a platform offering tokenized shares in more than 60 US-listed companies.

title: Franklin Templeton Clears Final Hurdle For ETFs That Turn Stock Dividends Into Bitcoin
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

Franklin Templeton Clears Final Hurdle For ETFs That Turn Stock Dividends Into Bitcoin
Franklin Templeton, the $1.7 trillion asset manager, registered two Nasdaq-listed funds yesterday. Both launch with a 95/5 split between U.S. stocks and bitcoin, and every dividend buys more bitc...
content:
Franklin Templeton has taken the last regulatory step before launching two exchange-traded funds that convert stock dividends into bitcoin. 

On October 22, Franklin Templeton filed a Form 8-A with the Securities and Exchange Commission to register shares of the Franklin US Equity Bitcoin DRIP Index ETF and the Franklin US Innovation Bitcoin DRIP Index ETF for trading on the Nasdaq. A prospectus filed the same day lists an effective date of October 27.

The filings for both funds arrived in June without tickers or fees. Four months later, the details are in.

How the funds work

The Equity fund, ticker FBEQ, tracks the VettaFi US Large-Cap 500 Bitcoin DRIP Index. The index holds the 500 largest U.S. companies by market capitalization, weighted by float-adjusted market cap. 

As of September 30, it held 499 stocks ranging from $10.2 billion to $5.5 trillion in size, with a concentration in information technology.

At inception, the index allocates 95% to those stocks and 5% to bitcoin. Each dividend the companies pay, regular or special, is reinvested into bitcoin at the market open on the day after the ex-date. The bitcoin share of the portfolio grows with each payment.

A traditional dividend reinvestment plan, or DRIP, buys more shares of the company that paid the dividend. Franklin’s version routes that cash into bitcoin. 

For a holder, the dividend stream from the largest companies in America becomes a recurring bitcoin purchase, with no exchange account, no wallet and no custody decisions.

The bitcoin position has limits. At each quarterly rebalance, an allocation above 5% is trimmed to 4.5%. If bitcoin exceeds 20% of the index between rebalances, it is cut back to 4.5% within two business days, and the proceeds return to stocks. The result is a stock fund with a bitcoin sleeve, not a bitcoin fund.

The ETF does not hold bitcoin on-chain. It gains exposure through bitcoin exchange-traded products, including Franklin’s own spot fund, through bitcoin futures and options, or through depositary receipts, in some cases via a Cayman Islands subsidiary.

FBEQ carries a 0.09% expense ratio with no 12b-1 fee. Franklin Advisory Services manages the fund, with Franklin Templeton Institutional as sub-advisor. Dina Ting, Hailey Harris, Joe Diederich and Basit Amin serve as portfolio managers.

The Innovation fund follows the same mechanic on the VettaFi US Innovation 100 Bitcoin DRIP Index, which draws from the 100 largest non-financial companies listed on the Nasdaq.

A deeper bet on bitcoin

Franklin Templeton filed for a spot bitcoin ETF in September 2023 and launched it as EZBC in January 2024. In April, the firm acquired 250 Digital and formed Franklin Crypto, an institutional digital asset division. Franklin Templeton CEO Jenny Johnson has argued that blockchains threaten Wall Street’s fee structure more than its technology.

The DRIP funds extend that strategy to investors who may never buy bitcoin on their own. A retiree holding an S&P 500-style fund in a brokerage account can, through FBEQ, let dividends from the companies she already owns build a bitcoin position over years.

The prospectus warns that investors can lose money, and that bitcoin’s price swings may affect the fund’s net asset value. Whether that trade-off appeals to the audience Franklin Templeton is targeting will become clear after October 27.

Micah Zimmerman

Micah first discovered Bitcoin in 2018 but remained a skeptic on the sidelines for too long. Since 2021, he has covered crypto and business and now works as a news reporter for Bitcoin Magazine, based in North Carolina.

title: Bitcoin seeks support above $81K as Brent crude oil hits highest level since March
summary: Bitcoin dipped below $81,000 as stocks fell and Brent crude hit its highest level since March, leaving the 50-day moving average in focus.
content:
Bitcoin (BTC) saw a fresh dip below $81,000 after Friday’s Wall Street open as Brent crude oil set new seven-month highs.

Key points:

  • Bitcoin briefly dropped below $81,000 at the start of Friday’s US trading session as stocks drifted lower and the US 10-year yield remained below 5%. 
  • Brent crude oil reached $116 per barrel for the first time since March 19 amid Middle East tensions.
  • BTC price action focused on reclaiming its 50-day simple moving average at $81,781.

US stocks slip, bond yields cool as oil surges

Data from TradingView showed BTC/USD falling to $80,988 before recovering to around $81,600 at the time of writing.

BTC/USD one-hour chart. Source: Cointelegraph/TradingView

US stocks opened lower as AI-sector expenditure woes coincided with a surge in oil prices on the back of tensions around the US-Iran war.

The S&P 500 and tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite Index were down 0.6% and 0.2%, respectively, at the time of writing. The Dow Jones Industrial Average was 1.4% lower.

As traders turned risk-averse, the 10-year US bond yield stayed below 5%, having reached 4.939% on Thursday, their lowest since Sept. 23.

US 10-year bond yield one-day chart. Source: Cointelegraph/TradingView 

Concerns that the US may renew military strikes on Iran around the midterm elections sent WTI crude oil past $102 per barrel on Friday. This is the highest level since Sept. 16. Brent crude saw an even sharper rise of nearly 3% to $116 per barrel, a level last seen in mid-March.

CFDs on Brent crude oil one-day chart. Source: Cointelegraph/TradingView

Commenting, economist Robin Brooks noted that prices were rising although oil flows through the Persian Gulf approached pre-war levels for many nations and Saudi Arabia surpassed its pre-war average.

“Since the start of the war, we’ve not seen this kind of decoupling between prices and flows,” he wrote in analysis on the day, seeing markets incorporating a “huge risk premium.”

Persian Gulf oil-transit volumes (screenshot). Source: Robin Brooks on Substack.com

BTC price analysis eyes 50-day trend line

Commenting on low-timeframe BTC price action, Keith Alan, cofounder of crypto trading platform Material Indicators, saw the potential for lower support retests to come.

Related: Here’s what happened in crypto today

BTC/USD, he noted, had fallen below its 50-day simple moving average (SMA) at $81,781, with bulls now attempting to reclaim it by the daily close.

“If they fail to do so by tonight’s close, I’m looking for a support test in the $78k - $80k range,” he told X followers.

BTC/USD one-day chart with 50 SMA. Source: Cointelegraph/TradingView

Previously, Cointelegraph reported on substantial BTC price support between $80,000 and $81,500, as this area hosts the aggregate cost basis for investors in the spot Bitcoin exchange-traded funds (ETFs).

title: 25 BLOOM Participants Join 3 Asian Central Banks to Advance Cross-Border Digital Money
summary:
Key Takeaways: Singapore, Malaysia, and Thailand are working together on cross-border settlement with digital money. Banks and technology companies join large crypto and payments companies like Ripple, Circle, Coinbase, and
The post 25 BLOOM Participants Join 3 Asian Central Banks to Advance Cross-B...
content:
Key Takeaways:

  • Singapore, Malaysia, and Thailand are working together on cross-border settlement with digital money.
  • Banks and technology companies join large crypto and payments companies like Ripple, Circle, Coinbase, and Visa for BLOOM.
  • The project addresses three issues: multi-jurisdictional settlement, interoperability of networks, and programmable compliance protocols.

Three central banks from the Southeast Asian region are sharing efforts to work together on digital money, and both traditional finance and the crypto industry are joining forces to enhance cross-border transactions. Singapore’s Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) announced on October 23 that Bank Negara Malaysia (BNM) and the Bank of Thailand (BOT) had joined its BLOOM initiative as policymaker members.

  • Three Central Banks Coordinate Digital Money Rules
  • Ripple, Circle and Coinbase Join a Growing Network
    • Three Priorities for Cross-Border Settlement
    • Lower Costs Could Support Institutional Crypto Adoption

Three Central Banks Coordinate Digital Money Rules

BLOOM is Borderless, Liquid, Open, Online and Multi-currency. The public-private effort aims to align thinking by regulators, financial institutions, payment networks, and technology providers about interborder digital money.

The project covers different forms of digital money, including tokenized bank deposits and regulated stablecoins. BLOOM is looking to make alternative arrangements, agree and work together and continue to respect the specific regulatory requirements for each jurisdiction.

This also applies to crypto markets, as fiat can fuel digital transfers and settlement, but this has to be followed with acceptance by counterparties, compatibility with infrastructure and adherence to local rules and laws.

The partnership also will serve to coordinate international standards and supervisory expectations, providing financial institutions with a more uniform approach to cross-border transactions, MAS said.

Read More: DBS and Citi Enable 24/7 USD Payments With Tokenized Deposits, Cutting Settlement to Minutes

Ripple, Circle and Coinbase Join a Growing Network

The new BLOOM members are Airwallex, Mastercard, Maybank, Monee, Nium, Ripple, ShopeePay, Visa and World Bank Group.

It brings on the existing participants including Circle, Coinbase, Anchorage Digital, DBS, J.P. Morgan, Standard Chartered, Stripe, Temasek, and other financial and tech companies. Hence, the project collects institutions that have experience in stablecoins, crypto infrastructure, banking, and international payments.

Three Priorities for Cross-Border Settlement

Within the course of this BLOOM participants will concentrate on the following three areas. They will look at how institutions can embrace diverse forms of digital money and complete transactions between their counterparties in different markets.

Second, they will be engaged in interoperability efforts, tackling the essential technical and operational challenges between the different payments systems and digital currencies. The third is the investigation of programmable controls, such as which can be installed in digital money transactions to verify identity, conduct sanctions screening, and ensure that the transactions are safe.

The issue with the faster digital transfers is not enough because these are vital for regulated stablecoins and tokenized deposits, as would the ability to accept, exchange and settle funds compliantly across jurisdictions.

Lower Costs Could Support Institutional Crypto Adoption

Common implementation frameworks and aligned commercial arrangements could streamline the need for financial institutions to have to negotiate individual processes with each counterparty or market, MAS said. That has the potential to reduce implementation costs and make new services available sooner.

World Bank Group involvement also adds a development viewpoint, such as through the introduction of modern payment mechanisms, cross-border payments, and greater access to finance.

title: Reflect Lets Anyone Launch a Solana Stablecoin in Under a Minute With Shared Yield
summary:
Key Takeaways: Reflect has released the Create tool, which enables the user to mint stablecoins with a brand on Solana in one go. Creators have discretion over the collateral accepted
The post Reflect Lets Anyone Launch a Solana Stablecoin in Under a Minute With Shared Yield appeared first on Crypto...
content:
Key Takeaways:

  • Reflect has released the Create tool, which enables the user to mint stablecoins with a brand on Solana in one go.
  • Creators have discretion over the collateral accepted and the allocation of underlying yields to the creators and token holders.
  • Solana claims that the launch process takes less than a minute.

Reflect has launched a new Solana-based tool that turns stablecoin creation into a near-instant process. The product, named Create, allows users to select collateral, incorporate their own branding, decide a yield-sharing plan, and create a stablecoin in a single transaction on a blockchain.

Create is live. Launch a stablecoin with your name on it, on @Solana, in one transaction.

Choose the collateral from a reviewed set and decide how the interest splits between you and your holders. Press build and the coin exists.

https://t.co/lwQ3rf33lJ https://t.co/MuqcgsrLJW

— Reflect (@reflectmoney) October 22, 2026

  • Reflect Turns Stablecoin Creation Into a One-Transaction Process
  • Creators Can Split Yield With Token Holders
    • Collateral Selection Determines How the Stablecoin Works

Reflect Turns Stablecoin Creation Into a One-Transaction Process

Reflect announced the launch of a new Create service on Solana, providing faster launch for businesses and developers of their own customizable stablecoins. Rather than developing token launch from scratch, users adopt any of the reviewed collaterals and set up the distribution plan for the gained revenue.

Finally, when it has been configured, it is built and the stablecoin is deployed to the Solana network. Solana’s Twitter account also added to the launch, stating that users would be able to secure their own stable coin within less than a minute.

Launch your own stablecoin on Solana in under a minute

— Solana (@solana) October 22, 2026

The product’s main focus is the emerging market of crypto companies, including their infrastructure, who desire a branded digital dollar without having to implement a reserve management system, token mechanics, and yield logic on their own.

Read More: Tesla’s $TSLA Stock Token Lands on Solana Across 10+ Apps via Backpack Securities

Creators Can Split Yield With Token Holders

The model of reflect, which is stablecoin, associates each stablecoin with yield-generating collateral. The creator determines the size of that return and whether it comes back to the holders or is kept by the issuer or application.

That makes it easy for any fintech, payment platform, marketplace, payroll provider, or crypto products to provide users with a brandable dollar asset while still earning a profit.

For example, a creator could direct most of the underlying yield to token holders while keeping a smaller portion as platform income. The following day’s return may vary due to the return produced by the cash held as collateral for the stablecoin.

Collateral Selection Determines How the Stablecoin Works

Reflect does not allow the creators to have any assets they want. Collateral should be sourced from a reviewed set that is assessed based on liquidity, asset quality and technical risk, according to the company.

Eligible assets must also be transferable and compatible with the user, meaning that there cannot be restrictions on their use onchain in any way. This means Create is not simply a token generator. The structure of the stablecoin is directly linked with assets behind the coins.

Additionally, liquidity in the venues underlying the redemption mechanism matters, and reserves might not be provisioned as readily during periods of market mayhem.

With its most recent addition, Create is further developing stablecoin infrastructure on the Solana payments and tokenization ecosystem.

title: Bank of Korea Wants Stablecoins Written Into Forex Law as Crypto Bill and Tax Fight Come to a Head
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

Bank of Korea Wants Stablecoins Written Into Forex Law as Crypto Bill and Tax Fight Come to a Head
The Bank of Korea told lawmakers it will draft a forex law amendment this year to regulate stablecoins as a means of payment, a plan that points to tighter cross-border controls rathe...
content:
The Bank of Korea plans to draft an amendment to the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act with the government before year-end that would regulate stablecoins as a means of payment, according to a written submission to the National Assembly’s annual audit reported by Korean outlet Digital Asset.

The central bank’s October 22 report, a follow-up to last year’s audit, says it is consulting with the government on measures to regulate cross-border transactions in virtual assets. 

While building a monitoring system based on foreign exchange network reporting, the bank said, it plans to prepare the amendment with the government this year to regulate stablecoins as a means of payment, among other aims.

That is a plan to write a bill, not a bill in itself. There is no draft text, no named token and no passage date. And “means of payment” is a defined term in Korean forex law: an instrument whose cross-border movement must be reported. 

On that reading, the amendment would put dollar stablecoins under the same controls as a wire to New York, not make them legal tender at a Seoul convenience store.

The BOK pointed to settlement outside the banking system, mixers and regulatory gaps around personal wallets as factors that ease illegal transactions. Bitcoin holders who self-custody in Korea should take note: the country’s capital controls are the reason the kimchi premium exists, and a tighter forex net around crypto would entrench those controls rather than ease them.

The forex work runs in parallel with the Digital Asset Basic Act, the licensing and stablecoin-issuance framework flagged alongside spot bitcoin ETF approval in the government’s 2026 growth strategy. 

Financial Services Commission chairman Lee Eog-weon told lawmakers Thursday that consultations are in their final stage and the bill will follow as soon as possible, Bloomingbit reported. 

The BOK said it will work with ministries to limit transactions that exploit the gap until that law exists.

South Korea’s crypto tax discussions

The gap has a date attached. Korea’s crypto income tax is due to take effect January 1, 2027, according to The Block, after three postponements, and lawmakers have questioned taxing a market before the law defining it is passed. 

Lee said Thursday the tax should “take various circumstances into full consideration,” per Yonhap. Democratic Party leader Kim Min-seok called Thursday for a “thorough final review,” a shift from a party that had insisted on 2027. 

Two petitions, one to repeal the tax and one to defer it two years, each cleared the 50,000 signatures that force a legislative review. 

The National Tax Service has not moved: it plans to finalize its draft tax notice by October 30, Digital Asset reported.

Micah Zimmerman

Micah first discovered Bitcoin in 2018 but remained a skeptic on the sidelines for too long. Since 2021, he has covered crypto and business and now works as a news reporter for Bitcoin Magazine, based in North Carolina.

title: SoFi Launches 4.40% APY Tokenized Deposit With FDIC Cover and 24/7 Crypto Access
summary:
Key Takeaways: SoFi launched a variable 4.40% APY tokenized bank deposit service named SOFIE. Each SOFIE signifies $1 deposited with SoFi Bank and is eligible for FDIC insurance up to
The post SoFi Launches 4.40% APY Tokenized Deposit With FDIC Cover and 24/7 Crypto Access appeared first on CryptoNi...
content:
Key Takeaways:

  • SoFi launched a variable 4.40% APY tokenized bank deposit service named SOFIE.
  • Each SOFIE signifies $1 deposited with SoFi Bank and is eligible for FDIC insurance up to a limit.
  • Users can use SOFIE 1:1 to get SoFiUSD, and then purchase and transact onchain all day.

SoFi is adding an interest-bearing layer to its crypto ecosystem with SOFIE, a tokenized deposit designed to keep digital dollars earning before users deploy them into crypto or blockchain payments.

The creation is a regulated bank deposit cum direct mixing with the bank’s dollar connected stablecoin, SoFiUSD.

  • SOFIE Pays 4.40% While Funds Stay in the Bank
  • SOFIE and SoFiUSD Serve Different Jobs
    • SoFi Targets Billions in Idle Digital Dollars
    • SoFi Builds a Bank-to-Blockchain Pipeline

SOFIE Pays 4.40% While Funds Stay in the Bank

There are $1,000 in each SOFIE. The check currently yields 4.40% annual percentage yield, although the minimum balance is not specified. The rate will vary over the course of time. In contrast to most crypto assets, SOFIE is not a payment stablecoin, but rather the deposit liability of SoFi Bank.

But that’s key as funds held by SOFIE are insured against loss through the FDIC, to the extent of applicable coverages, including the standard $250,000 per depositor per insured bank per ownership category coverage.

SoFi claims the product is for people that wish to create dollars ready for crypto sales, however non-accruing them sitting idle.

Read More: SEC Clears Path for Tokenized Stocks With 5-Year Onchain Trading Exemption

SOFIE and SoFiUSD Serve Different Jobs

SOFIE is designed to accrue interest. SoFiUSD is designed to transfer money. If users choose to deploy their funds, they can turn their SOFIE into SoFiUSD at a 1:1 ratio. SoFiUSD can be then used to buy cryptocurrencies directly from within the SoFi app or directly to any of the wallet options supported by blockchain rails at any time.

This way, users can get rewarded for their balances first, and then enter a stablecoin once placed onchain to find liquidity. SoFi reiterated that sofiUSD is not insured by the FDIC, nor are other digital assets.

SoFi Targets Billions in Idle Digital Dollars

The business is building SOFIE as an alternative to inactive balances of stablecoins. The research by the Federal Reserve, which SoFi referenced, suggested that around $64 billion (21.2%) of the market for stablecoins was stored in rarely used or inactive or forgotten wallets.

A user who may want to invest $5,000 into crypto may be able to probably put the cash in a SOFIE account where they accrue interest until they’re prepared to participate in a trade. At that time, the balance can be switched to crypto without needing to exit the SoFi ecosystem first to be converted into SoFiUSD.

Read More: Blockchain.com and NYSE Target 24/7 Tokenized Stocks for 44 Million Crypto Accounts

SoFi Builds a Bank-to-Blockchain Pipeline

It is SoFi’s fifth product launch regarding cryptocurrencies launched in under one year. In November 2025, the bank launched consumer crypto trading and now has over 40 cryptocurrencies available.

It introduced SoFiUSD for the 24/7 dollar movement and settlement a month later. The stablecoin is already leveraged by SoFi for settlements in its card program across Mastercard’s network worldwide, SoFi says.

The company is also introducing digital asset services for businesses, so corporate entities can provide and oversee fiat currency, stablecoin payments and other digital assets under one regulated entity.

SOFIE now adds an interest-bearing entry point to that system, letting customers earn on bank deposits before moving the same value into blockchain-based payments or crypto markets.

title: Here’s what happened in crypto today
summary: Need to know what happened in crypto today? Here is the latest news on daily trends and events impacting Bitcoin price, blockchain, DeFi, Web3 and crypto regulation.
content:
Today in crypto, China said its national blockchain should be mostly finished by 2030, Ethereum postponed the Glamsterdam testnet fork after and Bitcoin mining competition intensified as network hashrate reached a seven-month high despite the industry’s shift toward AI

China targets 2030 for its national blockchain network buildout

China has set a 2030 target for largely completing a national blockchain network under a five-year digital development plan published Friday.

The 15th Five-Year Plan for National Informatization, which sets priorities calls for deeper blockchain use in trade and finance in the Yangtze River Delta, and deployment at scale in manufacturing and agriculture in the Chengdu–Chongqing region in southwestern China.

Friday’s plan was issued by the Central Cyberspace Affairs Commission, a senior body within the ruling Communist Party that coordinates digital development policy.

The document makes the completion target explicit for a project already included in China’s national development plan released in March. A joint policy from the Communist Party’s central leadership and State Council published on Oct. 9 called for its construction.

Ethereum delays Glamsterdam Hoodi testnet launch over security risks

Ethereum developers have postponed the Glamsterdam hard fork on the Hoodi testnet after researchers identified gas-related security risks that could affect how existing smart contracts handle failed transactions.

The Ethereum Foundation (EF) said that the upgrade, originally scheduled for Oct. 26, would be delayed to allow developers to investigate how some proposals interact with smart contracts deployed on Ethereum. 

On Oct. 13, Blockchain security firm ChainSecurity warned that two proposals included in Glamsterdam, EIP-8037 and EIP-8038, could weaken safeguards against a type of attack called insufficient gas griefing. 

The postponement raises uncertainty over Glamsterdam’s mainnet timeline. Ethereum developers had been considering early December, with plans to finalize a schedule following successful Hoodi testing. 

Bitcoin mining competition heats up despite AI exodus

Bitcoin’s network hashrate has reached a seven-month high despite major mining companies shifting their computing capacity toward AI, signaling growing competition in the space, according to BlocksBridge Consulting.

Bitcoin’s seven-day average hashrate has climbed above 1 zettahash per second for the first time since March 3, suggesting that computing power leaving the network is being replaced by other miners.

Hashrate measures the computing power securing Bitcoin’s network, while mining difficulty determines how hard it is to earn new Bitcoin.

Mining difficulty increased 5.92% on Oct. 16, with BlocksBridge projecting another 5.16% increase at the next adjustment. Combined, that would represent an 11.4% increase across two adjustments, making it harder for miners to earn rewards.

The increase comes despite publicly traded mining companies reporting a 23% decline in realized hashrate as they redirect resources toward AI. Their AI-related revenue increased 52% quarter over quarter.

BlocksBridge estimates that roughly $1.5 billion worth of mining equipment has been displaced by the transition.

Some of that hardware may be finding new buyers among smaller miners with access to cheaper electricity, allowing them to expand operations while larger competitors pursue AI.

title: China targets 2030 for its national blockchain network buildout
summary: China’s five-year digital development plan calls for wider blockchain use in trade and manufacturing alongside stronger technical standards.
content:
China’s five-year digital development plan calls for wider blockchain use in trade and manufacturing alongside stronger technical standards.

China has set a 2030 target for largely completing a national blockchain network under a five-year digital development plan published Friday.

The 15th Five-Year Plan for National Informatization, which sets priorities calls for deeper blockchain use in trade and finance in the Yangtze River Delta, and deployment at scale in manufacturing and agriculture in the Chengdu–Chongqing region in southwestern China.

Friday’s plan was issued by the Central Cyberspace Affairs Commission, a senior body within the ruling Communist Party that coordinates digital development policy.

The document makes the completion target explicit for a project already included in China’s national development plan released in March. A joint policy from the Communist Party’s central leadership and State Council published on Oct. 9 called for its construction.

The new plan also calls for stronger blockchain technical standards and greater use of the technology in data circulation and trading.

Mainland China bans cryptocurrency-related business activities, but promotes blockchain technology as a national priority.

In October 2019, President Xi Jinping called for greater investment in blockchain and identified it as an important area for developing China’s own technological capabilities.

title: Coinbase Ireland Hit With €3.25M Fine Over Fund Safeguarding and Oversight Failures
summary:
Key Takeaways: Irish central bank fines Coinbase Ireland $1.19m for customer fund safeguarding and outsourcing failures. The company used too much information from its U.S. parent group, while its local
The post Coinbase Ireland Hit With €3.25M Fine Over Fund Safeguarding and Oversight Failures appe...
content:
Key Takeaways:

  • Irish central bank fines Coinbase Ireland $1.19m for customer fund safeguarding and outsourcing failures.
  • The company used too much information from its U.S. parent group, while its local experience with the oversight side lacked, the regulator said.
  • A settlement discount of 30% resulted in the penalty being reduced to €4.65m, but still needs confirmation by the High Court.

Ireland’s central bank has imposed a fine of €3.25m on Coinbase’s Irish subsidiary for lacklustre measures to keep customer funds safe and for oversight of outsourced operations in the region. Breaches took place from November 2020 to August 2025 and related to the rules for electronic money institutions.

  • Coinbase Ireland Failed to Fully Safeguard Customer Funds
  • Heavy Reliance on Coinbase’s U.S. Group Raised Oversight Concerns
    • €4.65M Penalty Drops to €3.25M After Settlement
    • Irish Regulator Tightens Focus on Crypto-Linked Financial Firms

Coinbase Ireland Failed to Fully Safeguard Customer Funds

Coinbase Ireland Limited is an electronic money institution within the Coinbase Group.

Safeguarding controls are an important aspect of Coinbase’s regulated activities as it offers users e-money through an Irish division to buy or sell crypto assets on its trading platform.

The Central Bank of Ireland found that Coinbase Ireland’s systems and control testing were not strong enough to ensure customer funds were fully protected. The regulator says the company has been depositing funds into a designated safeguarding account for a long time that hasn’t been sufficient.

Weaknesses are also identified in the internal escalation and governance processes as part of the enforcement action. Coinbase Ireland did not have adequate processes to identify and report material safeguarding changes to the regulator.

Read More: Coinbase Joins 4-Day Crackdown on West Africa Crypto Scams and Asset Freezes

Heavy Reliance on Coinbase’s U.S. Group Raised Oversight Concerns

Probably one of the key issues was outsourcing. The Irish unit was heavily reliant on the U.S.-based Coinbase Group for the safeguarding of processes and controls necessary under Irish and EU rules.

The Central Bank, however, did not believe that Coinbase Ireland had the necessary local skills and expertise to adequately manage those functions. The regulator stressed that outsourcing does not remove a licensed firm’s responsibility for protecting customers.

€4.65M Penalty Drops to €3.25M After Settlement

Initially the Central Bank decided a reprimand and financial penalty of €4,646,597 was warranted.

It acknowledged the regulatory flaws but accepted the undisputed facts, meaning it had the benefit of the maximum 30% discount available under the settlement process available.

That cut down the final fine to just €3 252 618. The sanctions will be effective from a designated date that is still to come. They still have to be confirmed by Ireland’s High Court. The court will uphold the penalty under the country’s administrative sanctions system if the court considers the sanction to be manifestly disproportionate.

Irish Regulator Tightens Focus on Crypto-Linked Financial Firms

It exemplifies the importance of traditional financial protections in companies that offer infrastructure for cryptocurrency trading. Companies doing business in Ireland need to have the skills, governance and internal controls to safeguard customers’ interests, Central Bank Enforcement Director Karen O’Leary said.

Special attention to obligations made during the authorization was given to commitments that also take effect after the authorization, particularly if they lead to access to the EU’s broader market.

The Central Bank issued its 164th enforcement outcome in its enforcement history, with over €432 million of fines resulting from enforcement actions to date.

title: BNB Price Prediction: $1.2B Token Burn Fuels Bullish Hopes as BNB Tests Critical $750 Resistance
summary: BNB is approaching a key technical decision point near $750 after BNB Chain permanently removed more than 1.64 million tokens from circulation in its latest quarterly burn.
content:
Skip to content
Assets: BNB

BNB is approaching a key technical decision point near $750 after BNB Chain permanently removed more than 1.64 million tokens from circulation in its latest quarterly burn.

The supply reduction supports BNB’s long-term deflationary design, but the price must overcome resistance to strengthen the bullish outlook.

BNB traded around $730–$745 in late October 2026 after briefly testing the $750 area. Technical analysts are watching whether the token can break above the upper boundary of its multi-month range or retreat toward lower support levels. The recent burn adds a fundamental development to that chart-based debate, although it does not guarantee an immediate price increase.

BNB’s $1.2 Billion Token Burn Reduces Supply

BNB Chain completed its 37th quarterly auto-burn on October 19, permanently removing 1,646,196.44 BNB valued at approximately $1.197 billion at the time of the announcement. The BNB Foundation reported that the remaining total supply stood at 131,512,085 tokens.

CZ reposted BNB Chain’s announcement of the 37th quarterly auto-burn, confirming 1,646,196 BNB tokens valued at approximately $1.197 billion were permanently removed from circulation. Source: @cz_binance via X

The burn is part of BNB’s long-term plan to reduce its total supply to 100 million tokens. The Auto-Burn mechanism calculates the amount removed using factors that include BNB’s price and block production on BNB Smart Chain. The tokens are sent to an inaccessible burn address, taking them out of circulation.

However, the $1.2 billion valuation does not represent fresh buying or money spent on a market buyback. The dollar figure reflects the estimated value of the tokens at the time of the burn. CryptoSlate reported that the number of tokens removed increased by approximately 1.9% compared with the July burn, while the reported dollar value rose by 28.5%, largely reflecting the higher implied value per token.

The reduction in supply supports BNB’s deflationary design, but its effect on market price depends on demand, trading activity, and selling pressure. The burn alone does not establish that buyers are entering the market or that BNB will break through resistance.

$750 Resistance Becomes the Key BNB Price Level

Market analyst Alex Marzell has identified the $750 area as a critical level for BNB, describing it as a potential “make or break zone” near the top of the token’s multi-month trading range.

A sustained move above this area could strengthen the case for a recovery toward previous highs and potentially new all-time highs. Such a move would need confirmation from continued buying pressure and follow-through rather than a brief intraday spike.

BNB is retesting key resistance near $750, with a hold potentially paving the way to new all-time highs, while a breakdown could trigger a decline toward a higher-timeframe demand zone. Source: @MarzellCrypto via X

Recent market data reinforces the importance of this threshold. On October 22, technical analysis placed immediate resistance near $752.78, with support around $722.52. The daily relative strength index (RSI) was approximately 45, indicating that momentum remained below the neutral 50 level rather than showing strong bullish conviction. 

For the bullish scenario to gain traction, the price would need to reclaim the $750–$753 region and sustain trading above it. A confirmed breakout could open the way toward the next resistance areas, although the price would still face potential selling pressure as it approaches higher levels.

Failure to clear resistance would leave BNB vulnerable to another pullback within its broader range. The token’s reaction around $750 is therefore more important than the burn’s headline valuation when assessing its immediate technical direction.

BNB Price Forecast: Can the $680–$695 Demand Zone Hold?

Analyst TokenTalk3x has highlighted the $680–$695 region as a potential demand zone if BNB retreats from current levels. The area is being monitored as a possible location for buyers to return, rather than a confirmed price floor.

BNB’s $680–$695 demand zone could offer an accumulation opportunity during pullbacks, despite traders’ tendency to favor rallies over dips. Source: @TokenTalk3x via X

The analysis identifies a Change of Character (CHoCH), a technical term used to describe a possible shift in market structure. If the price pulls back into the highlighted zone and rebounds with stronger buying activity, the chart setup points to a possible recovery toward $850.

That target remains conditional. Traders would need to see evidence that buyers are defending the zone, such as a clear price reaction and improving momentum. A decline through the area could instead expose lower support levels.

The setup also highlights a common difference between trading a breakout and buying a pullback. Chasing a sharp upward move can leave traders entering close to resistance, while waiting for a retracement may offer a clearer level for evaluating risk. Neither approach guarantees a profitable outcome.

Head-and-Shoulders Pattern Raises Risk of a Deeper BNB Correction

A separate daily-chart analysis by TradingView contributor AnhbaCong_ presents a more bearish interpretation. The analyst suggests BNB may be forming a head-and-shoulders reversal pattern, with the head near $815 and the neckline around $700.

BNB is nearing completion of a daily head-and-shoulders reversal pattern, with the right shoulder forming around $745–$750 after a decline from the $815 peak toward the $700 neckline. Source: AnhbaCong_ on TradingView

In this formation, the right shoulder has developed near $745–$750. The analysis points to rejection around $748 and a subsequent retreat toward $730 as evidence that sellers remain active near resistance. It also identifies declining volume during the right-shoulder formation as a potential sign of weakening buying participation.

The bearish scenario would gain credibility if the price breaks below the $700 neckline with sustained selling pressure. The analyst identifies $600 as a potential downside objective if the pattern is confirmed. However, the formation is not complete simply because the price has retreated from resistance, and a move above the right shoulder could weaken the bearish interpretation.

The analysis also outlines an early short setup with a stop-loss above $748.39. That is the contributor’s trading strategy, not an established market outcome. Attempting to anticipate a breakdown before confirmation carries additional risk if BNB instead recovers above resistance.

The contrasting projections illustrate why the $700 and $750 levels matter. A breakout above resistance would weaken the immediate bearish case, while a confirmed neckline breakdown would increase the risk of a more substantial correction.

BNB Price Outlook: What Comes Next?

BNB’s outlook rests on the interaction between supply reduction and price action. The October burn permanently removed more than 1.64 million tokens, but the market has yet to demonstrate that this development will be enough to push the price above its immediate resistance zone.

BNB price chart. Source: Brave New Coin

The bullish scenario requires a sustained break above $750–$753, which could bring higher resistance levels and the $850 target identified in one technical analysis into focus. The bearish scenario involves rejection near resistance followed by a break below $700, potentially strengthening the case for a deeper retracement.

Between those levels, the $680–$695 demand zone remains an area to watch for evidence of renewed buying. RSI readings near neutral territory and conflicting chart patterns suggest that a decisive move has yet to be established.

For now, the $1.2 billion BNB burn provides a long-term supply narrative, while resistance near $750 remains the immediate technical test. A confirmed breakout or breakdown would offer stronger evidence of the next directional move than the burn announcement alone.

title: Born2trade CEO: “Everything is about gold now. Gold traders dictate industry standards and features”
summary:
Gold has lost about a quarter of its value since January, the Fed is hiking, and retail traders are more focused on the metal than ever. After 25 years in brokerage, here is what I think that means for traders and for the brokers who serve them.
Gold trades around $4,100–4,200 an ounce, roughly 24% ...
content:
Gold has lost about a quarter of its value since January, the Fed is hiking, and retail traders are more focused on the metal than ever. After 25 years in brokerage, here is what I think that means for traders and for the brokers who serve them.

Gold trades around $4,100–4,200 an ounce, roughly 24% below the record near $5,600 it set at the end of January, according to CIBC Capital Markets. The Federal Reserve is raising rates, not cutting them. By the old textbook, this should be a quiet time for gold.

However, it is not. In my more than 25 years in brokerage and trading, I have rarely seen retail clients this concentrated on one instrument. In our experience, and from what we see across the industry, between 70% and sometimes 90% of retail clients trade gold. That is a fact no broker can afford to ignore.

Why everyone trades gold

Nobody can give a precise answer to this, so I can only share how I see it. We live in a very complicated environment: geopolitical events, the war in Ukraine, uncertainty in the Middle East, and inflationary pressure that has kept building since COVID. Market participants — and simply people, are cautious about everything around them. Absolutely everything.

I read the total concentration on gold as a lack of trust in broader markets and investment instruments.

Gold stays the clearest asset for investors and traders, even though it is anything but clear when it comes to predicting its price.

The big money appears to agree. Central banks bought 345 tonnes of gold in the first half of 2026, according to World Gold Council data cited by CIBC, and gold-backed ETFs attracted a record $30.7 billion in the third quarter.

For brokers, the lesson is simple. The market and traders dictate what matters. A broker has to listen to its clients and build every development around their needs — not around its own dreams and ideas. That is how business works, and in 2026 the clients are telling us, very clearly, that they want gold.

Gold has no P/E ratio, and no obvious floor

Is gold expensive or cheap? From a classic valuation point of view, gold is much harder to judge than the S&P 500, the Nasdaq, or any asset with earnings, a P/E ratio, or similar measures. Honestly speaking, gold can cost $1,000–3,000, or $4,000–6,000 and higher. Naming a floor is far more complicated than for any equity index.

January showed how quickly sentiment can turn. Gold set a record of about $5,595 an ounce on 29 January. The next day it fell more than 9% — its sharpest one-day drop since 1983 — after Kevin Warsh was named as the next Fed Chair. By late June it had slipped below $4,000, roughly 29% off the high. And yet, compared with what markets are capable of, that crash was nothing.

So what is my estimate? I am convinced gold will stay one of the most actively traded assets through the end of 2026, and most likely through 2027. Over a one-year horizon, I see plenty of reasons for it to fluctuate anywhere between $3,000 and $6,000 if something truly unpredictable happens.

The forces on each side are clear. The Fed’s rate path and its fight with inflation — the Fed raised rates by 25 basis points in September, and the 10-year Treasury yield is above 5% — are calming bullish sentiment. Global risks, uncertainty, and central bank demand are helping the bulls. I expect this balance to continue for the next few quarters. For reference, CIBC now forecasts $4,500 for the fourth quarter and an average of $5,200 in 2027.

I watched Lehman collapse on my trading screen

What about stocks, indices, and AI? I see a lot of signs of a bubble, and similarities with the dot-com era and even the 2008 crisis.

I remember 2008 not from textbooks but from my monitor. I watched Lehman Brothers collapse through the trading platform. I watched the S&P and the Nasdaq fall while the Japanese yen rose in record steps in September that year.

The new wave of traders, many of whom have only known rising markets, needs to study this history, be aware of it, and be prepared. For many years, financial markets have mostly been in rise mode, with very short-lived corrections. That will not last forever, and traders must understand it.

There is another side to this. Being ready for big swings is good for active traders, because the biggest opportunities come in exactly those periods — together with the biggest risks.

What active gold traders demand from a broker

If I had to put it in one word, it would be flexibility. It starts with how clients deposit, runs through trading conditions and leverage, and ends with how they withdraw.

Money moving to a broker and out of a broker must be fast, even ultra-fast. Right now there is no faster or more flexible route than crypto deposits and withdrawals. Even open banking and cards are not that friendly for active traders and investors.

Trading conditions must be just as flexible. Active clients need to hold positions at low cost, react quickly, and sit more comfortably through turbulence. That is why brokers are now competing on the cost of holding gold overnight, on the choice of leverage and on loyalty schemes, not only on spreads. At Born2trade, for example, we have answered this with positive overnight swaps on long gold positions and a gold-linked loyalty programme. We also offer a separate low-commission, fast-execution account for traders who care most about speed. The direction is set by clients, not by us.

How to choose a broker in a turbulent market

In simple words, trade with a broker you feel comfortable with. That is the main criterion.

Regulation plays a growing role in that choice. Brokers regulated by Tier-1 and Tier-2 authorities are more and more often the first choice for clients, and for objective reasons: stronger investor protection, clearer rules, and more confidence in how client money is handled. That is a real competitive advantage, and clients see it. Still, regulation alone is not a 100% guarantee that a broker is fair, or that it fits you and your trading style.

Group reputation and openness to the public are key factors in judging how reliable your broker is. The company’s owners and top management should not be hidden. They should be open and reachable, and trading conditions should be clear and genuinely beneficial to clients.

More important than anything else, though, is one rule: the initiative to trade must come from the client.

It is great when a broker promotes good, competitive conditions — that is what competition is for. But there should be no promises of fast profits and no pushy sales at all. A solid, fair and legal broker will never push anyone, least of all a beginner, by calling constantly or pressuring them. The initiative must come from the trader, all the time.

Gold discipline and a clear mind

Gold will keep testing traders in both directions over the coming quarters. The brokers that win will be the ones that listen to those traders and build around what they actually need. The traders who win will be the ones who respect the risk as much as the opportunity.

My wish for every trader, and every gold trader in particular, is simple: gold discipline and a clear mind.

Konstantin Rashap is CEO and Co-founder of Born2trade, an online broker offering trading in currencies, metals, commodities, indices, stocks and cryptocurrencies on MetaTrader 5. He has more than 25 years of experience in the brokerage industry and in trading.

The views expressed are the author’s own and are for information only. They are not investment advice or a price forecast. Trading CFDs and other leveraged products carries a high risk of losing money rapidly.

Gold will keep testing traders in both directions over the coming quarters. The brokers that win will be the ones that listen to those traders and build around what they actually need. The traders who win will be the ones who respect the risk as much as the opportunity.

My wish for every trader, and every gold trader in particular, is simple: gold discipline and a clear mind.

Konstantin Rashap is CEO and Co-founder of Born2trade, an online broker offering trading in currencies, metals, commodities, indices, stocks and cryptocurrencies on MetaTrader 5. He has more than 25 years of experience in the brokerage industry and in trading.

The views expressed are the author’s own and are for information only. They are not investment advice or a price forecast. Trading CFDs and other leveraged products carries a high risk of losing money rapidly.

title: What’s Really Going on Behind the Scenes of a Brokerage?
summary:
Trading technology has evolved considerably over the past decade. But has it evolved enough?
The January 2021 GameStop short squeeze was a watershed moment for the entire brokerage industry, making brokers brutally aware of how vulnerable their trading systems can be when activity peaks. 
Five years...
content:
2026-10-23T10:37:06.299+02:00

Friday, 23/10/2026 | 08:37 GMT by Finctra

Disclaimer

  • As geopolitics continues to drive market sentiment, trading activity is at its height. Brokers face the dilemma of widening their spreads to mitigate market risk or absorbing the cost of keeping spreads stable to satisfy traders.
  • Risk management technology provider Finctra begs to differ. According to a spokesperson, “Execution quality and margin protection should not be a trade-off. Brokers must have a clear picture of their exposure to reduce risk and prevent profit bleeding.”

Trading technology has evolved considerably over the past decade. But has it evolved enough?

The January 2021 GameStop short squeeze was a watershed moment for the entire brokerage industry, making brokers brutally aware of how vulnerable their trading systems can be when activity peaks.

Five years down the line, same story, different setting. Through predatory practices such as bonus abuse or cross-account arbitrage, traders continue to test brokerage systems, pushing them to the brink of collapse. Without clear visibility into such activities, brokers remain risk prone.

According to Finctra, the problem is “operational” and “systemic”. “To contain risk, brokers must still be able to identify it. Real-time visibility on potentially anomalous activity can help brokers spot intent before it becomes harmful," the spokesperson said.

The multiple facets of Finctra risk management

From an infrastructural perspective, many trading platform operators still run on disparate systems. From compliance to risk and trade reporting, every team uses different technologies. This leads to data fragmentation, with each team ending up with a fractured view of what happens on the other side of the trade. Finctra proposes a lucrative, system-driven solution.

Marketed as an institutional-grade risk management infrastructure, Finctra can help brokers continuously monitor and control risk while ensuring operational stability. Thanks to its multilevel capabilities, Finctra can monitor, detect, alert and respond to risk-threatening incidents in real time.

Built for MT4 and MT5 environments, Finctra’s technology suite can help streamline brokerage operations end-to-end, eliminating complexities from each core function, as follows:

  • RiskGuard helps monitor exposure and supports informed response in real time
  • Finctra Hub supports acumen by providing brokerage teams with a clear view of exposure and trading performance
  • OpsCenter equips MT4/MT5 admin and operations teams with the right tools to manage swap and tick data updates, handle batches or lots, and other recurring tasks hassle-free.

This layered platform architecture promotes a hierarchical yet unified view of brokerage operations in real time, qualifying Finctra as a brokerage risk intelligence partner for FX and CFD brokers. This is what makes it relevant across a variety of use cases.

Use case 1: Identifying margin risk

When volatility peaks, trading activity intensifies, increasing volume in specific instruments and amplifying brokerage exposure. Imagine the Fed changed its interest rate, surprising the markets to the upside. USD goes up against most of its major peers. Traders go long and short on most USD-based pairs and alternative assets, but one particular account holds multiple one-sided positions in EURUSD. This trader’s heavy exposure threatens to trigger margin call failures, generating negative balance risks.

Finctra’s RiskGuard can track this type of exposure in real time across individual accounts and multi-account clusters simultaneously. This flexibility allows teams to track both single large trades and the rapid accumulation of trading volume within short time windows.

Because a standard rule focused only on individual trade sizes might miss a high-volume threshold reached through multiple smaller trades, RiskGuard allows risk professionals to configure risk parameters based clear monitoring criteria, varying from individual large trades to volume accumulation over a short period of time. These parameters include trade sizes, specific time windows, order counts, and cumulative lots, all scoped to relevant account groups and symbols.

When a configured condition is met, RiskGuard automatically triggers an alert detailing the affected account, symbol, trade direction, specific trigger criteria, and timestamp. These data-driven, actionable insights help brokerage teams narrow down the possible activity triggers and formulate the appropriate response.

Use case 2: Understanding exposure and trading performance

To offer competitive pricing, brokers rely on multiple liquidity providers. During high-impact economic events like the NFP or central bank announcements, brokerage teams may notice concentrated exposure in specific symbols, such as XAUUSD or DJI. As traders respond to price spikes, the volume on these ticks increases drastically, with order books growing thinner by the hour.

The Finctra Hub addresses these challenges by providing a consolidated view on risk exposure and the overall trading activity carried out through the platform. By tracking multiple liquidity providers, Finctra enables appropriate position matching and facilitates reconciliation and trade reporting.

With a high-level overview of long and short positions, net exposure by symbol, and currency exposure analysis, dealers or risk managers can identify concentrations and review P&L and trading activity by trading account, symbol and country. This provides a solid basis for investigation, operational planning and decision-making.

The Country Analysis tool, for example, offers a unified view of country-level P&L, trading accounts and traded lots over a selected period. This level of detail enables teams to compare activities and results across different client markets and identify areas that warrant a closer look. Combined with broader trade intelligence, country-specific data informs regional planning and resource allocation.

The Hub’s functionality is enhanced by the Liquidity Connectivity and Infrastructure tools, which allow brokers to expand their liquidity pools across global venues while maintaining execution quality and stability. This level of flexibility enables risk professionals to streamline reporting, improve efficiency and acumen.

Use case 3: Simplifying platform administration

Market conditions change rapidly, and MT4 and MT5 brokers feel the pressure firsthand. To remain competitive and compliant, platform administrators must update swaps, apply configuration changes across multiple symbol groups, and ensure tick data is up-to-date.

These tasks can be time-consuming, and switching between different systems doesn’t make it more efficient. This is where the OpsCenter can make a difference. Designed to eliminate manual work and streamline processes for platform administrators, Finctra’s OpsCenter improves efficiency and reduces the risk of manual work-related errors in areas including:

  • Batch management & configuration: Instead of updating configurations symbol-by-symbol, platform admins can group assets by class, server and group type. OpsCenter allows users to select targeted symbol sets and apply configuration templates simultaneously.

  • Swap updates: Changing central bank policies affect currency prices and market liquidity, making swap rate updates necessary. The OpsCenter features swap update tools that enable swift batch swap updates for selected symbols, recording the values before and after each change, along with its success status, to enable straightforward review and tracking.

Trading technology has evolved considerably over the past decade. But has it evolved enough?

The January 2021 GameStop short squeeze was a watershed moment for the entire brokerage industry, making brokers brutally aware of how vulnerable their trading systems can be when activity peaks.

Five years down the line, same story, different setting. Through predatory practices such as bonus abuse or cross-account arbitrage, traders continue to test brokerage systems, pushing them to the brink of collapse. Without clear visibility into such activities, brokers remain risk prone.

According to Finctra, the problem is “operational” and “systemic”. “To contain risk, brokers must still be able to identify it. Real-time visibility on potentially anomalous activity can help brokers spot intent before it becomes harmful," the spokesperson said.

The multiple facets of Finctra risk management

From an infrastructural perspective, many trading platform operators still run on disparate systems. From compliance to risk and trade reporting, every team uses different technologies. This leads to data fragmentation, with each team ending up with a fractured view of what happens on the other side of the trade. Finctra proposes a lucrative, system-driven solution.

Marketed as an institutional-grade risk management infrastructure, Finctra can help brokers continuously monitor and control risk while ensuring operational stability. Thanks to its multilevel capabilities, Finctra can monitor, detect, alert and respond to risk-threatening incidents in real time.

Built for MT4 and MT5 environments, Finctra’s technology suite can help streamline brokerage operations end-to-end, eliminating complexities from each core function, as follows:

  • RiskGuard helps monitor exposure and supports informed response in real time
